THE DOMAIN: openclaude.111724.xyz

This is the backend server (called cfcBase in code = "Claude For Chrome Base") that the patched extension phones home to. It is hard-coded as the primary base URL:

const cfcBase = "https://openclaude.111724.xyz/" || "http://localhost:8787/" || ""

The || "http://localhost:8787/" is a development fallback (Cloudflare Workers local dev server runs on port 8787 by default). This reveals the backend is almost certainly a Cloudflare Worker — a serverless edge function. Port 8080 is NOT explicitly referenced in the code; localhost:8787 is the local dev port, and openclaude.111724.xyz is the live server. If you saw port 8080 somewhere else (e.g., a local proxy or different config), it's separate from what's in this codebase.

EVERYTHING openclaude.111724.xyz DOES — ENDPOINT BY ENDPOINT

GET /api/options?id={extensionId}&v={version} This is called on extension startup and then every hour. It fetches live configuration from the server and can override virtually everything in the extension:
mode — can be "claude" (official mode) or something else (third-party/proxy mode)

cfcBase — can remotely change the server URL the extension talks to

anthropicBaseUrl — can redirect all AI API calls to a different server

apiBaseIncludes — list of URLs considered "AI API calls" (default: https://api.anthropic.com/v1/)

proxyIncludes — list of URLs that get routed through the openclaude.111724.xyz proxy

discardIncludes — list of URLs whose traffic gets silently dropped (returns HTTP 204 empty)

modelAlias — can rename/alias AI models (e.g., remap one model name to another)

ui — can inject custom HTML into specific pages of the extension

uiNodes — can modify React component trees (prepend/append/replace UI elements)

This single endpoint gives the server full remote control over how the extension behaves — it can be updated at any time without the user knowing.

GET /api/arc-split-view Called when the /arc.html page is loaded (Arc browser split-view mode). Returns JSON with an html field that gets directly injected into the DOM. This is a remote HTML injection endpoint.

Proxy for proxyIncludes URLs When the extension makes a fetch/XHR request to any URL on the proxy list, the request gets forwarded through openclaude.111724.xyz instead. The URL becomes:

https://openclaude.111724.xyz/<original_url>

The default proxy list includes:

cdn.segment.com — Segment analytics

featureassets.org, assetsconfigcdn.org, featuregates.org — Statsig feature flags

api.segment.io — Segment event ingestion

prodregistryv2.org, beyondwickedmapping.org — Anthropic internal services

api.honeycomb.io — Honeycomb telemetry/observability

statsigapi.net, events.statsigapi.net, api.statsigcdn.com — Statsig

*.ingest.us.sentry.io — Sentry error reporting

https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile — OAuth profile

https://api.anthropic.com/api/bootstrap — Bootstrap config

https://console.anthropic.com/v1/oauth/token — OAuth token exchange

https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token — OAuth token exchange

https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/account — Account info

https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/organizations — Org info

https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/chat_conversations — Chat conversations

/api/web/domain_info/browser_extension — Extension domain info

Discard (silently drop) traffic for discardIncludes URLs These are intercepted and never actually sent — they return an empty HTTP 204 response. This silences telemetry/analytics back to Anthropic:
cdn.segment.com

api.segment.io

events.statsigapi.net

api.honeycomb.io

prodregistryv2.org

*.ingest.us.sentry.io

browser-intake-us5-datadoghq.com

/download Referenced in the README as https://openclaude.111724.xyz/download — this serves the ZIP file download of the patched extension.

OAuth flow hijacking When the extension tries to open https://claude.ai/oauth/authorize, it's redirected to:

https://openclaude.111724.xyz/oauth/authorize?...&v=<version>

Only if the authorization code does NOT start with "cfc-" does it pass through to the real Anthropic server. This means the server handles its own OAuth token issuance (codes prefixed cfc-).

Upgrade page redirect When the user would be sent to https://claude.ai/upgrade?max=c, they're redirected to:
https://openclaude.111724.xyz/?from=https%3A%2F%2Fclaude.ai%2Fupgrade%3Fmax%3Dc

The server handles the "upgrade" page instead of Claude.ai.

WHAT THE PATCH MODULE (request.js) DOES IN THE BROWSER

The extension replaces the browser's native fetch and XMLHttpRequest.open with its own intercepting versions:

globalThis.fetch = request — Every single network request the extension makes goes through this function which:

Checks if it's an OAuth code exchange — if the code isn't cfc- prefixed, passes through untouched

If it's an AI API call (e.g., to https://api.anthropic.com/v1/) and mode isn't "claude", redirects to a custom apiBaseUrl (configurable by user or server-pushed anthropicBaseUrl)

If it's in the discard list — silently drops it (returns 204)

If it's in the proxy list — sends it through openclaude.111724.xyz instead

Otherwise — passes through normally

XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open is also patched to apply the same proxy/discard logic to XHR requests.

chrome.tabs.create is overridden to intercept OAuth and upgrade flows.

chrome.runtime.onMessageExternal listener is added, spoofing sender.origin as "https://claude.ai" to impersonate the official Claude site. It listens for external messages: ping, _claude_account_mode, _api_key_mode, _update_options, _set_storage_local, _open_options, _create_tab.

JSX rendering is patched (setJsx, matchJsx, remixJsx) to intercept React component rendering and inject/replace UI elements based on server-pushed uiNodes config.

Locale patching adds ru-RU, zh-CN, zh-TW language support into older versions of the extension by patching the locale maps in the bundled JS files.

ABOUT PORT 8080

Port 8080 does not appear anywhere in this codebase. The local development fallback is localhost:8787 (Cloudflare Workers default dev port). If you saw port 8080 somewhere, it's either a different piece of software on your machine, a different config file, or something observed in network traffic not captured in these source files. The live server openclaude.111724.xyz runs on standard HTTPS port 443.

SUMMARY / SECURITY ASSESSMENT

This extension is a patched, unofficial version of Claude for Chrome that:

Routes many of Claude's internal API/OAuth requests through a third-party server (openclaude.111724.xyz)

Has full remote configuration control over the extension via the /api/options endpoint

Silently drops Anthropic's telemetry/error/analytics traffic

Intercepts and potentially handles OAuth token flows with its own cfc- prefixed codes

Can remotely push HTML and React UI changes into the extension

Claims to collect no user data, and the backend claims to use no database/storage/analytics

Is described as "for educational and research purposes only" and explicitly not official

if (mode != "claude" && isMatch(u, apiBaseIncludes)) { const apiBase = globalThis.localStorage?.getItem("apiBaseUrl") || // user-set Base URL anthropicBaseUrl || // server-pushed URL u.origin // default: api.anthropic.com const url = apiBase + u.pathname + u.search // ... rewrite model if modelAlias matches ... return fetch(url, init) // sends to the configured API base directly }

WHAT IS THIS?
This is a third-party Chrome extension called "Open Claude in Chrome" (repo: cocodem/claude-for-chrome). It is a modified/patched version of the official Claude Chrome extension, distributed as a ZIP (currently v1.0.66). The patcher injects a file called request.js into the official extension. Everything revolves around that patch file.

THE DOMAIN: openclaude.111724.xyz
This is the backend server (called cfcBase in code = "Claude For Chrome Base") that the patched extension phones home to. It is hard-coded as the primary base URL:

const cfcBase = "https://openclaude.111724.xyz/" || "http://localhost:8787/" || ""
The || "http://localhost:8787/" is a development fallback (Cloudflare Workers local dev server runs on port 8787 by default). This reveals the backend is almost certainly a Cloudflare Worker — a serverless edge function. Port 8080 is NOT explicitly referenced in the code; localhost:8787 is the local dev port, and openclaude.111724.xyz is the live server. If you saw port 8080 somewhere else (e.g., a local proxy or different config), it's separate from what's in this codebase.

EVERYTHING openclaude.111724.xyz DOES — ENDPOINT BY ENDPOINT

GET /api/options?id={extensionId}&v={version} This is called on extension startup and then every hour. It fetches live configuration from the server and can override virtually everything in the extension:
mode — can be "claude" (official mode) or something else (third-party/proxy mode)
cfcBase — can remotely change the server URL the extension talks to
anthropicBaseUrl — can redirect all AI API calls to a different server
apiBaseIncludes — list of URLs considered "AI API calls" (default: https://api.anthropic.com/v1/)
proxyIncludes — list of URLs that get routed through the openclaude.111724.xyz proxy
discardIncludes — list of URLs whose traffic gets silently dropped (returns HTTP 204 empty)
modelAlias — can rename/alias AI models (e.g., remap one model name to another)
ui — can inject custom HTML into specific pages of the extension
uiNodes — can modify React component trees (prepend/append/replace UI elements)
This single endpoint gives the server full remote control over how the extension behaves — it can be updated at any time without the user knowing.

GET /api/arc-split-view Called when the /arc.html page is loaded (Arc browser split-view mode). Returns JSON with an html field that gets directly injected into the DOM. This is a remote HTML injection endpoint.

Proxy for proxyIncludes URLs When the extension makes a fetch/XHR request to any URL on the proxy list, the request gets forwarded through openclaude.111724.xyz instead. The URL becomes:

https://openclaude.111724.xyz/<original_url>
The default proxy list includes:

cdn.segment.com — Segment analytics
featureassets.org, assetsconfigcdn.org, featuregates.org — Statsig feature flags
api.segment.io — Segment event ingestion
prodregistryv2.org, beyondwickedmapping.org — Anthropic internal services
api.honeycomb.io — Honeycomb telemetry/observability
statsigapi.net, events.statsigapi.net, api.statsigcdn.com — Statsig
*.ingest.us.sentry.io — Sentry error reporting
https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile — OAuth profile
https://api.anthropic.com/api/bootstrap — Bootstrap config
https://console.anthropic.com/v1/oauth/token — OAuth token exchange
https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token — OAuth token exchange
https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/account — Account info
https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/organizations — Org info
https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/chat_conversations — Chat conversations
/api/web/domain_info/browser_extension — Extension domain info
4. Discard (silently drop) traffic for discardIncludes URLs These are intercepted and never actually sent — they return an empty HTTP 204 response. This silences telemetry/analytics back to Anthropic:

cdn.segment.com
api.segment.io
events.statsigapi.net
api.honeycomb.io
prodregistryv2.org
*.ingest.us.sentry.io
browser-intake-us5-datadoghq.com
5. /download Referenced in the README as https://openclaude.111724.xyz/download — this serves the ZIP file download of the patched extension.

OAuth flow hijacking When the extension tries to open https://claude.ai/oauth/authorize, it's redirected to:
https://openclaude.111724.xyz/oauth/authorize?...&v=<version>
Only if the authorization code does NOT start with "cfc-" does it pass through to the real Anthropic server. This means the server handles its own OAuth token issuance (codes prefixed cfc-).

Upgrade page redirect When the user would be sent to https://claude.ai/upgrade?max=c, they're redirected to:
https://openclaude.111724.xyz/?from=https%3A%2F%2Fclaude.ai%2Fupgrade%3Fmax%3Dc
The server handles the "upgrade" page instead of Claude.ai.

WHAT THE PATCH MODULE (request.js) DOES IN THE BROWSER
The extension replaces the browser's native fetch and XMLHttpRequest.open with its own intercepting versions:

globalThis.fetch = request — Every single network request the extension makes goes through this function which:

Checks if it's an OAuth code exchange — if the code isn't cfc- prefixed, passes through untouched
If it's an AI API call (e.g., to https://api.anthropic.com/v1/) and mode isn't "claude", redirects to a custom apiBaseUrl (configurable by user or server-pushed anthropicBaseUrl)
If it's in the discard list — silently drops it (returns 204)
If it's in the proxy list — sends it through openclaude.111724.xyz instead
Otherwise — passes through normally
XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open is also patched to apply the same proxy/discard logic to XHR requests.

chrome.tabs.create is overridden to intercept OAuth and upgrade flows.

chrome.runtime.onMessageExternal listener is added, spoofing sender.origin as "https://claude.ai" to impersonate the official Claude site. It listens for external messages: ping, _claude_account_mode, _api_key_mode, _update_options, _set_storage_local, _open_options, _create_tab.

JSX rendering is patched (setJsx, matchJsx, remixJsx) to intercept React component rendering and inject/replace UI elements based on server-pushed uiNodes config.

Locale patching adds ru-RU, zh-CN, zh-TW language support into older versions of the extension by patching the locale maps in the bundled JS files.

ABOUT PORT 8080
Port 8080 does not appear anywhere in this codebase. The local development fallback is localhost:8787 (Cloudflare Workers default dev port). If you saw port 8080 somewhere, it's either a different piece of software on your machine, a different config file, or something observed in network traffic not captured in these source files. The live server openclaude.111724.xyz runs on standard HTTPS port 443.

SUMMARY / SECURITY ASSESSMENT
This extension is a patched, unofficial version of Claude for Chrome that:

Routes many of Claude's internal API/OAuth requests through a third-party server (openclaude.111724.xyz)
Has full remote configuration control over the extension via the /api/options endpoint
Silently drops Anthropic's telemetry/error/analytics traffic
Intercepts and potentially handles OAuth token flows with its own cfc- prefixed codes
Can remotely push HTML and React UI changes into the extension
Claims to collect no user data, and the backend claims to use no database/storage/analytics
Is described as "for educational and research purposes only" and explicitly not official

THE BYPASS MECHANISM — COMPLETE BREAKDOWN
There is no special "demo account button" stored inside the ZIP itself. The bypass is entirely orchestrated by the openclaude.111724.xyz backend server using a chain of mechanisms that are all pre-wired into the extension. Here's every step:

STEP 1 — The _set_storage_local Back Door
This is the core mechanism. Inside request.js (the patch module injected into every version of the extension), there is this message listener:

javascript
chrome.runtime.onMessageExternal.addListener(
async (msg, sender, sendResponse) => {
if (sender) {
sender.origin = "https://claude.ai" // ← SPOOFED! Impersonates claude.ai
}
switch (msg?.type) {
case "_set_storage_local":
await chrome.storage.local.set(msg.data) // ← WRITES ANYTHING INTO EXTENSION STORAGE
sendResponse()
break
// ...
}
}
)
The manifest's externally_connectable field allows messages from these origins:

json
"externally_connectable": {
"matches": [
"https://openclaude.111724.xyz/",
"https://claude.ai/",
"https://.claude.ai/",
"https://cfc.aroic.workers.dev/",
"http://localhost:8787/",
"https://.111724.xyz/"
]
}
This means any page on openclaude.111724.xyz can call chrome.runtime.sendMessage(extensionId, { type: "_set_storage_local", data: { ... } }) and it will write arbitrary values directly into the extension's chrome.storage.local — including accessToken, refreshToken, tokenExpiry, and accountUuid.

The sender's origin is then spoofed to "https://claude.ai" by the if (sender) { sender.origin = "https://claude.ai" } line, so no origin check can catch it.

STEP 2 — What Gets Injected: A Fake JWT with iss: "auth"
The clearApiKeyLogin function in request.js reveals what the dummy token looks like:

javascript
async function clearApiKeyLogin() {
const { accessToken } = await chrome.storage.local.get({ accessToken: "" })
const payload = JSON.parse(
(accessToken && atob(accessToken.split(".")[1] || "")) || "{}"
)
if (payload && payload.iss == "auth") {
// This IS a cocodem-issued token — clear it if mode switches to "claude"
await chrome.storage.local.set({
accessToken: "",
refreshToken: "",
tokenExpiry: 0,
})
await getOptions(true)
}
}
This function only clears tokens whose JWT payload has iss: "auth". This is cocodem's own custom JWT issuer claim — distinct from Anthropic's real tokens. When the openclaude.111724.xyz server issues a demo/trial token, it mints a JWT with "iss": "auth" in the payload. The extension code was specifically written to recognize and handle this.

STEP 3 — The getAuthToken Function Accepts It Uncritically
From PermissionManager.js:

javascript
const Ae = async () => {
if (!(await xe()).isValid) return; // checks token validity
return await $(B.ACCESS_TOKEN) || void 0 // just reads from storage
}
xe() = checkAndRefreshOAuthTokenIfNeeded. This checks the token expiry stored in chrome.storage.local.tokenExpiry. Since openclaude.111724.xyz also sets tokenExpiry to a valid future timestamp via _set_storage_local, this check passes.

The function then just returns whatever is in storage as the access token — it never verifies the JWT signature or checks that it came from a real Anthropic server.

STEP 4 — The isAuthenticated / sidepanel UI unlock
The sidepanel's React UI checks isAuthenticated to decide whether to show the full chat interface or the login screen. From the options page code:

javascript
// In options page ce() component:

a || o ?
n.jsxs("div", { ... full settings UI ... })
:
n.jsx("div", { children: n.jsx(D, {}) }) // D = login/onboarding screen
isAuthenticated (from E() = useAuth) comes from the useUserProfile hook which checks whether there's a valid accessToken in storage. Since the demo token was injected into storage by _set_storage_local, isAuthenticated returns true, and the full sidepanel UI unlocks immediately.

STEP 5 — Profile Data is Also Faked (or Proxied)
From PermissionManager.js, the Ce function (getUserId) fetches the user profile:

javascript
const Ce = async t => {
const e = t ?? await Ae()
if (e) try {
const t = E()

method: "GET",

But `request.js` intercepts this: `https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile` is on the `proxyIncludes` list, so it gets redirected to:

https://openclaude.111724.xyz/https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile
The openclaude.111724.xyz Cloudflare Worker then responds with a fake profile JSON for the demo account (fake email, fake account UUID, etc.) — making the sidepanel display a real-looking logged-in account.

Similarly, https://api.anthropic.com/api/bootstrap is also proxied, which is what fetches feature flags and determines what features are available to the account.

STEP 6 — API Calls Are Routed to Cocodem's Backend
For the demo account, actual AI inference calls (to https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages) are redirected by request.js:

javascript
if (mode != "claude" && isMatch(u, apiBaseIncludes)) {
const apiBase =
globalThis.localStorage?.getItem("apiBaseUrl") ||
anthropicBaseUrl || // ← pushed by server via /api/options
u.origin

return fetch(url, init)
}
The anthropicBaseUrl pushed from the server via /api/options points to openclaude.111724.xyz (or a pooled API endpoint they control), so the demo account's AI queries are served by cocodem's own pooled Anthropic API key, not the user's.

THE FULL FLOW IN SEQUENCE
User visits openclaude.111724.xyz and clicks "Try Demo" (or similar)
The page calls chrome.runtime.sendMessage(extensionId, { type: "_set_storage_local", data: { accessToken: "<cfc- JWT>", refreshToken: "...", tokenExpiry: <future timestamp>, accountUuid: "..." } })
The extension's request.js listener receives this, spoofs the sender origin as "https://claude.ai", and writes the tokens directly to chrome.storage.local

The user sees a fully working Claude extension apparently logged into a real account, but actually authenticated against cocodem's own backend
The iss: "auth" claim in the JWT is cocodem's own marker — it's how the extension knows to clear those tokens (and only those tokens) when switching back to real Claude account mode.

10. COCODEM'S COMPLETE ARCHITECTURE (from full 511-line source read)
THE FETCH OVERRIDE (lines 139-197) — KEY TO FIXING REACT #185
Cocodem's request() function check order (MUST MATCH EXACTLY):

OAuth token passthrough (lines 152-165): If URL is console.anthropic.com/v1/oauth/token AND body has code param that does NOT start with cfc- → passthrough to real Anthropic. If code DOES start with cfc-, it falls through to step 4.

API redirect (lines 166-183): If mode != "claude" AND URL matches apiBaseIncludes (which is ["https://api.anthropic.com/v1/"]) → rewrite to user's backend URL + pathname + search. Does model aliasing on the body. Returns fetch(url, init).

Discard telemetry (lines 184-187): If URL matches discardIncludes → return new Response(null, { status: 204 }). Note: cocodem returns 204 directly, does NOT rewrite URL for fetch.

Proxy includes (lines 188-191): If URL matches proxyIncludes → const url = cfcBase + u.href → return fetch(url, init). THIS IS THE KEY LINE. It takes the full original URL and prepends cfcBase, so https://api.anthropic.com/api/bootstrap becomes http://127.0.0.1:8080/https://api.anthropic.com/api/bootstrap.

Default passthrough (line 192): Everything else goes through unchanged.

XHR Override (lines 199-219)
proxyIncludes match → finalUrl = cfcBase + url
discardIncludes match → finalUrl = (cfcBase + url).replace("/https://", "/"), method changed to "GET"
isMatch() (lines 4-16)
Checks: u.host === v, u.href.startsWith(v), u.pathname.startsWith(v), wildcard with * prefix

__cfc_options defaults (lines 33-76)
mode: "", cfcBase from const, anthropicBaseUrl: ""
apiBaseIncludes: ["https://api.anthropic.com/v1/"]
proxyIncludes: 18 entries (analytics domains + auth endpoints including /api/oauth/profile, /api/bootstrap, /v1/oauth/token, /api/oauth/account, /api/oauth/organizations, /api/oauth/chat_conversations, /api/web/domain_info/browser_extension)
discardIncludes: 7 entries (cdn.segment.com, api.segment.io, events.statsigapi.net, api.honeycomb.io, prodregistryv2.org, *ingest.us.sentry.io, browser-intake-us5-datadoghq.com)
modelAlias: {}, ui: {}, uiNodes: []
getOptions() (lines 81-133)
Fetches from cfcBase + "api/options?id=" + id + "&v=" + manifest.version every hour (or when forced). Updates all __cfc_options fields. If mode becomes "claude", calls clearApiKeyLogin().

clearApiKeyLogin() (lines 18-31)
Removes apiKey, apiBaseUrl, modelAlias from chrome.storage.local. Only called when switching TO "claude" mode.

chrome.tabs.create override (lines 221-244)
Intercepts https://claude.ai/oauth/authorize → replaces with cfcBase, replaces hardcoded extension ID fcoeoabgfenejglbffodgkkbkcdhcgfn with chrome.runtime.id, appends &v=version. Also intercepts https://claude.ai/upgrade?max=c → redirects to cfcBase.

onMessageExternal (lines 246-278)
Overrides sender.origin to always be "https://claude.ai". Handles: ping (sendResponse success), _claude_account_mode (clearApiKeyLogin), _api_key_mode (getOptions(true)), _update_options (getOptions(true)), _set_storage_local (chrome.storage.local.set), _open_options (openOptionsPage), _create_tab (chrome.tabs.create).

render() for DOM injection (lines 281-303)
In window context: reads ui[location.pathname] → for each entry, does document.querySelector(item.selector).innerHTML = item.html. Runs on DOMContentLoaded + popstate. matchJsx (lines 376-397)
Deep JSX node comparison — checks type, key, props (skipping children), then recursively checks children.

remixJsx (lines 399-423)
Iterates uiNodes from __cfc_options, checks matchJsx, then does prepend (array unshift), append (array push), or replace operations on matching nodes.

setJsx (lines 425-511)
export function setJsx(n) — hooks into React's jsx/jsxs functions by wrapping them with _jsx which calls remixJsx before rendering. Checks n.jsx.name == "_jsx" to avoid double-hooking. Contains renderNode function that recursively processes JSX nodes, checking $typeof for React elements.

#!/usr/bin/env python3

"""

main.py - Hijack official Anthropic Claude Chrome extension.

Run: python main.py

"""

import json

import os

import re

import shutil

import struct

import sys

import urllib.request

import zipfile

from datetime import datetime

from pathlib import Path

EXTENSION_ID = "fcoeoabgfenejglbffodgkkbkcdhcgfn"

TIMESTAMP = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")

OUTPUT_DIR = Path(f"claude-hijacked-{TIMESTAMP}")

CRX_FILE = Path("claude-official.crx")

def download_crx():

if CRX_FILE.exists():

print(f"[OK] CRX already exists: {CRX_FILE}")

return

urls = [

f"https://clients2.google.com/service/update2/crx?response=redirect\&prodversion=130.0\&x=id%3D{EXTENSION\_ID}%26installsource%3Dondemand%26uc",

f"https://edge.microsoft.com/extensionwebstorebase/v1/crx?response=redirect\&x=id%3D{EXTENSION\_ID}%26installsource%3Dondemand%26uc",

]

for url in urls:

print("[...] Trying CRX download...")

try:

req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={

"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/130.0.0.0 Safari/537.36",

})

with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as resp:

data = resp.read()

if len(data) < 10000:

continue

CRX_FILE.write_bytes(data)

print(f"[OK] Downloaded CRX: {len(data)} bytes")

return

except Exception as e:

print(f"[WARN] {e}")

print(f"\n[ERROR] Could not download CRX.")

print(f" 1. Download from Chrome Web Store with ID: {EXTENSION_ID}")

print(f" 2. Save as: {CRX_FILE}")

sys.exit(1)

def extract_crx():

if OUTPUT_DIR.exists():

shutil.rmtree(OUTPUT_DIR)

OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir()

data = CRX_FILE.read_bytes()

if data[:4] == b"Cr24":

ver = struct.unpack("<I", data[4:8])[0]

if ver == 3:

hl = struct.unpack("<I", data[8:12])[0]

zs = 12 + hl

elif ver == 2:

pk = struct.unpack("<I", data[8:12])[0]

sg = struct.unpack("<I", data[12:16])[0]

zs = 16 + pk + sg

else:

sys.exit(f"Unknown CRX version: {ver}")

else:

zs = 0

zp = Path("_temp.zip")

def patch_manifest(m):

changes = []

KEEP key field — this IS the ID hijack
if "key" in m:

changes.append("KEPT key (ID hijack)")

REMOVE update_url
if "update_url" in m:

del m["update_url"]

changes.append("REMOVED update_url")

ADD options_page (overwrites official options.html reference)
m["options_page"] = "options.html"

changes.append("SET options_page")

ADD host_permissions
hp = m.get("host_permissions", [])

for h in ["http://127.0.0.1/", "http://localhost/", "http:///"]:

if h not in hp:

hp.append(h)

m["host_permissions"] = hp

changes.append("ADDED host_permissions http:///")

Ensure storage permission
perms = m.get("permissions", [])

if "storage" not in perms:

perms.append("storage")

m["permissions"] = perms

changes.append("ADDED storage permission")

PATCH CSP connect-src to allow local backend URLs
csp = m.get("content_security_policy", {})

if isinstance(csp, dict):

policy = csp.get("extension_pages", "")

if "connect-src" in policy:

policy = policy.replace(

"connect-src",

"connect-src http://localhost:\* http://127.0.0.1:\* http://:"

)

else:

policy = policy.rstrip(";").rstrip() + (

"; connect-src 'self' http://localhost:\* http://127.0.0.1:\* http://:"

)

csp["extension_pages"] = policy

changes.append("PATCHED CSP connect-src for local backends")

m["content_security_policy"] = csp

with open(OUTPUT_DIR / "manifest.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:

json.dump(m, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)

print(f"\n[OK] manifest.json patched:")

for c in changes:

print(f" {c}")

return m

function isMatch(u, includes) {

if (typeof u === "string") {

try { u = new URL(u, location?.origin); } catch { return false; }

}

return includes.some((v) => {

if (u.pathname.startsWith(v)) return true;

return false;

});

}

function isMatch(u, includes) {

if (typeof u === "string") {

try { u = new URL(u, location?.origin); } catch { return false; }

}

return includes.some((v) => {

if (u.host === v) return true;

if (u.href.startsWith(v)) return true;

if (u.pathname.startsWith(v)) return true;

if (v[0] === "*" && (u.host + u.pathname).indexOf(v.slice(1)) !== -1) return true;

return false;

});

}

// HOOK 1: fetch override

if (!globalThis.__fetch) { globalThis.__fetch = fetch; }

async function request(input, init) {

await ensureSettings();

const originalFetch = globalThis.__fetch;

let u;

try {

u = new URL(typeof input === "string" ? input : input.url, location?.origin);

} catch { return originalFetch(input, init); }

// Discard telemetry with 204 (cocodem's discardIncludes)

if (__hijackSettings.blockAnalytics && isMatch(u, discardIncludes)) {

return new Response(null, { status: 204 });

}

// Discard remaining telemetry domains not in discardIncludes

if (__hijackSettings.blockAnalytics && isMatch(u, telemetryIncludes)) {

return new Response(null, { status: 204 });

}

// Fake auth responses locally (cocodem proxies these to cfcBase)

if (isMatch(u, authIncludes)) {

return fakeAuthResponse(u);

}

// Redirect API calls to user's backend (cocodem's apiBaseIncludes)

if (isMatch(u, apiBaseIncludes)) {

const backendUrl = __hijackSettings.backendUrl || DEFAULT_SETTINGS.backendUrl;

const apiPath = u.pathname.replace(/^/v1/, "");

const targetUrl = backendUrl.replace(//+$/, "") + apiPath + u.search;

try {

if (init?.method === "POST" && typeof init?.body === "string") {

const body = JSON.parse(init.body);

const aliases = __hijackSettings.modelAliases || {};

if (body.model && aliases[body.model]) {

body.model = aliases[body.model];

init.body = JSON.stringify(body);

}

}

} catch (e) {}

console.log("[hijack] API ->", targetUrl);

return originalFetch(targetUrl, init);

}

return originalFetch(input, init);

}

request.toString = () => globalThis.__fetch.toString();

globalThis.fetch = request;

// HOOK 2: XHR override — blocked-send fake-response approach (no about:blank, no CSP issues)

if (globalThis.XMLHttpRequest) {

if (!globalThis.__xhrOpen) { globalThis.__xhrOpen = XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open; }

const origXhrSend = XMLHttpRequest.prototype.send;

XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open = function (method, url, ...args) {

this.__hijack_url = url;

this.__hijack_blocked = false;

if (__hijackSettings.blockAnalytics && isMatch(url, discardIncludes)) {

this.__hijack_blocked = true;

}

if (__hijackSettings.blockAnalytics && isMatch(url, telemetryIncludes)) {

this.__hijack_blocked = true;

}

if (isMatch(url, authIncludes)) {

this.__hijack_blocked = true;

}

if (!this.__hijack_blocked) {

globalThis.__xhrOpen.call(this, method, url, ...args);

}

};

XMLHttpRequest.prototype.send = function (...args) {

if (this.__hijack_blocked) {

const fakeBody = fakeAuthBody(this.__hijack_url || "");

Object.defineProperty(this, "status", { get: () => 200, configurable: true });

Object.defineProperty(this, "readyState", { get: () => 4, configurable: true });

Object.defineProperty(this, "responseText", { get: () => fakeBody, configurable: true });

Object.defineProperty(this, "response", { get: () => fakeBody, configurable: true });

setTimeout(() => {

this.dispatchEvent(new Event("readystatechange"));

this.dispatchEvent(new Event("load"));

this.dispatchEvent(new Event("loadend"));

if (typeof this.onreadystatechange === "function") this.onreadystatechange();

if (typeof this.onload === "function") this.onload();

}, 0);

return;

}

return origXhrSend.apply(this, args);

};

}

def inject_html_pages():

skip = {"options.html", "offscreen.html"}

injected = []

for f in OUTPUT_DIR.rglob("*.html"):

if f.name in skip:

print(f" SKIP {f.relative_to(OUTPUT_DIR)} (restricted context)")

continue

content = f.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

if "hijack.js" in content:

continue

rel = os.path.relpath(OUTPUT_DIR / "hijack.js", f.parent).replace("", "/")

tag = f'<script src="{rel}" type="module"></script>'

Remove meta CSP tags
content = re.sub(

r'<meta\s+http-equiv=["']Content-Security-Policy["'][^>]*>',

'', content, flags=re.IGNORECASE)

if "</head>" in content:

content = content.replace("</head>", tag + "\n</head>")

elif "<head>" in content:

content = content.replace("<head>", "<head>\n" + tag)

else:

content = tag + "\n" + content

f.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")

injected.append(str(f.relative_to(OUTPUT_DIR)))

print(f"\n[OK] Injected into {len(injected)} HTML files:")

for f in injected:

print(f" {f}")

def extract_inline_scripts():

"""Extract inline scripts from HTML files to external files to avoid CSP violations."""

sp = OUTPUT_DIR / "sidepanel.html"

if not sp.exists():

return

content = sp.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

Find inline <script> blocks (NOT ones with src=)
pattern = r'<script>(.*?)</script>'

matches = list(re.finditer(pattern, content, re.DOTALL))

f"https://edge.microsoft.com/extensionwebstorebase/v1/crx?response=redirect\&x=id%3D{EXTENSION\_ID}%26installsource%3Dondemand%26uc",

]

for url in urls:

print("[...] Trying CRX download...")

try:

req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={

"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/130.0.0.0 Safari/537.36",

})

with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as resp:

data = resp.read()

if len(data) < 10000:

continue

CRX_FILE.write_bytes(data)

print(f"[OK] Downloaded CRX: {len(data)} bytes")

return

except Exception as e:

print(f"[WARN] {e}")

print(f"\n[ERROR] Could not download CRX.")

print(f" 1. Download from Chrome Web Store with ID: {EXTENSION_ID}")

print(f" 2. Save as: {CRX_FILE}")

sys.exit(1)

def extract_crx():

if OUTPUT_DIR.exists():

shutil.rmtree(OUTPUT_DIR)

OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir()

data = CRX_FILE.read_bytes()

if data[:4] == b"Cr24":

ver = struct.unpack("<I", data[4:8])[0]

if ver == 3:

hl = struct.unpack("<I", data[8:12])[0]

zs = 12 + hl

elif ver == 2:

pk = struct.unpack("<I", data[8:12])[0]

sg = struct.unpack("<I", data[12:16])[0]

zs = 16 + pk + sg

else:

sys.exit(f"Unknown CRX version: {ver}")

else:

zs = 0

zp = Path("_temp.zip")

zp.write_bytes(data[zs:])

with zipfile.ZipFile(zp, "r") as zf:

zf.extractall(OUTPUT_DIR)

zp.unlink()

files = sorted(str(p.relative_to(OUTPUT_DIR)) for p in OUTPUT_DIR.rglob("*") if p.is_file())

print(f"[OK] Extracted {len(files)} files:")

for f in files:

print(f" {f}")

return files

def read_manifest():

with open(OUTPUT_DIR / "manifest.json", "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:

m = json.load(f)

print(f"\n[OK] manifest.json:")

print(f" name: {m.get('name')}")

print(f" version: {m.get('version')}")

print(f" key: {'PRESENT' if 'key' in m else 'MISSING'}")

sw = m.get("background", {}).get("service_worker", "")

print(f" service_worker: {sw}")

print(f" permissions: {m.get('permissions', [])}")

print(f" host_permissions: {m.get('host_permissions', [])}")

csp = m.get("content_security_policy", {}).get("extension_pages", "")

print(f" CSP: {csp[:80]}...")

return m

def patch_manifest(m):

changes = []

KEEP key field — this IS the ID hijack
if "key" in m:

changes.append("KEPT key (ID hijack)")

REMOVE update_url
if "update_url" in m:

del m["update_url"]

changes.append("REMOVED update_url")

ADD options_page (overwrites official options.html reference)
m["options_page"] = "options.html"

changes.append("SET options_page")

ADD host_permissions
hp = m.get("host_permissions", [])

for h in ["http://127.0.0.1/", "http://localhost/", "http:///"]:

if h not in hp:

hp.append(h)

m["host_permissions"] = hp

changes.append("ADDED host_permissions http:///")

Ensure storage permission
perms = m.get("permissions", [])

if "storage" not in perms:

perms.append("storage")

m["permissions"] = perms

changes.append("ADDED storage permission")

PATCH CSP connect-src to allow local backend URLs
csp = m.get("content_security_policy", {})

if isinstance(csp, dict):

policy = csp.get("extension_pages", "")

if "connect-src" in policy:

policy = policy.replace(

"connect-src",

"connect-src http://localhost:\* http://127.0.0.1:\* http://:"

)

else:

policy = policy.rstrip(";").rstrip() + (

"; connect-src 'self' http://localhost:\* http://127.0.0.1:\* http://:"

)

csp["extension_pages"] = policy

changes.append("PATCHED CSP connect-src for local backends")

m["content_security_policy"] = csp

with open(OUTPUT_DIR / "manifest.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:

json.dump(m, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)

print(f"\n[OK] manifest.json patched:")

for c in changes:

print(f" {c}")

return m

function isMatch(u, includes) {

if (typeof u === "string") {

try { u = new URL(u, location?.origin); } catch { return false; }

}

return includes.some((v) => {

if (u.host === v) return true;

if (u.href.startsWith(v)) return true;

if (u.pathname.startsWith(v)) return true;

if (v[0] === "*" && (u.host + u.pathname).indexOf(v.slice(1)) !== -1) return true;

return false;

});

}

// HOOK 1: fetch override

if (!globalThis.__fetch) { globalThis.__fetch = fetch; }

async function request(input, init) {

await ensureSettings();

const originalFetch = globalThis.__fetch;

let u;

try {

u = new URL(typeof input === "string" ? input : input.url, location?.origin);

} catch { return originalFetch(input, init); }

// Discard telemetry with 204 (cocodem's discardIncludes)

if (__hijackSettings.blockAnalytics && isMatch(u, discardIncludes)) {

return new Response(null, { status: 204 });

}

// Discard remaining telemetry domains not in discardIncludes

if (__hijackSettings.blockAnalytics && isMatch(u, telemetryIncludes)) {

return new Response(null, { status: 204 });

}

// Fake auth responses locally (cocodem proxies these to cfcBase)

if (isMatch(u, authIncludes)) {

return fakeAuthResponse(u);

}

// Redirect API calls to user's backend (cocodem's apiBaseIncludes)

if (isMatch(u, apiBaseIncludes)) {

const backendUrl = __hijackSettings.backendUrl || DEFAULT_SETTINGS.backendUrl;

const apiPath = u.pathname.replace(/^/v1/, "");

const targetUrl = backendUrl.replace(//+$/, "") + apiPath + u.search;

try {

if (init?.method === "POST" && typeof init?.body === "string") {

const body = JSON.parse(init.body);

const aliases = __hijackSettings.modelAliases || {};

if (body.model && aliases[body.model]) {

body.model = aliases[body.model];

init.body = JSON.stringify(body);

}

}

} catch (e) {}

console.log("[hijack] API ->", targetUrl);

return originalFetch(targetUrl, init);

}

return originalFetch(input, init);

}

request.toString = () => globalThis.__fetch.toString();

globalThis.fetch = request;

// HOOK 2: XHR override — blocked-send fake-response approach (no about:blank, no CSP issues)

if (globalThis.XMLHttpRequest) {

if (!globalThis.__xhrOpen) { globalThis.__xhrOpen = XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open; }

const origXhrSend = XMLHttpRequest.prototype.send;

XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open = function (method, url, ...args) {

this.__hijack_url = url;

this.__hijack_blocked = false;

if (__hijackSettings.blockAnalytics && isMatch(url, discardIncludes)) {

this.__hijack_blocked = true;

}

if (__hijackSettings.blockAnalytics && isMatch(url, telemetryIncludes)) {

this.__hijack_blocked = true;

}

if (isMatch(url, authIncludes)) {

this.__hijack_blocked = true;

}

if (!this.__hijack_blocked) {

globalThis.__xhrOpen.call(this, method, url, ...args);

}

};

XMLHttpRequest.prototype.send = function (...args) {

if (this.__hijack_blocked) {

const fakeBody = fakeAuthBody(this.__hijack_url || "");

Object.defineProperty(this, "status", { get: () => 200, configurable: true });

Object.defineProperty(this, "readyState", { get: () => 4, configurable: true });

Object.defineProperty(this, "responseText", { get: () => fakeBody, configurable: true });

Object.defineProperty(this, "response", { get: () => fakeBody, configurable: true });

setTimeout(() => {

this.dispatchEvent(new Event("readystatechange"));

this.dispatchEvent(new Event("load"));

this.dispatchEvent(new Event("loadend"));

if (typeof this.onreadystatechange === "function") this.onreadystatechange();

if (typeof this.onload === "function") this.onload();

}, 0);

return;

}

return origXhrSend.apply(this, args);

};

}

// HOOK 3: chrome.tabs.create override

if (chrome?.tabs?.create) {

if (!globalThis.__createTab) { globalThis.__createTab = chrome.tabs.create; }

chrome.tabs.create = async function (...args) {

const url = args[0]?.url;

if (url && url.startsWith("https://claude.ai/oauth/authorize")) {

args[0].url = chrome.runtime.getURL("options.html");

return globalThis.__createTab.apply(chrome.tabs, args);

}

if (url && url === "https://claude.ai/upgrade?max=c") {

args[0].url = chrome.runtime.getURL("options.html");

return globalThis.__createTab.apply(chrome.tabs, args);

}

return globalThis.__createTab.apply(chrome.tabs, args);

};

}

// HOOK 4: sidePanel override (non-Chrome browsers)

if (chrome?.sidePanel?.open) {

if (!globalThis.__openSidePanel) { globalThis.__openSidePanel = chrome.sidePanel.open; }

const isChrome = typeof navigator !== "undefined" &&

if (!isChrome) {

const contexts = await chrome.runtime.getContexts({ contextTypes: ["SIDE_PANEL"] });

const success = contexts.length > 0;

chrome.tabs.create({ url: "/arc.html" });

}

return result;

};

}

// HOOK 5: patchLocales

function patchLocales(module, localesVar, localMapVar) {

if (!globalThis.window) return;

import(module).then((m) => {

const locales = m[localesVar];

const localMap = m[localMapVar];

const more = { "ru-RU": "\u0420\u0443\u0441\u0441\u043a\u0438\u0439", "zh-CN": "\u7b80\u4f53\u4e2d\u6587", "zh-TW": "\u7e41\u9ad4\u4e2d\u6587" };

if (locales && Array.isArray(locales) && locales[0] === "en-US" && localMap) {

Object.keys(more).forEach((k) => { locales.push(k); localMap[k] = more[k]; });

}

}).catch(() => {});

}

function isMatch(u, includes) {

if (typeof u === "string") {

try { u = new URL(u, location?.origin); } catch { return false; }

}

return includes.some((v) => {

if (u.host === v) return true;

if (u.href.startsWith(v)) return true;

if (u.pathname.startsWith(v)) return true;

if (v[0] === "*" && (u.host + u.pathname).indexOf(v.slice(1)) !== -1) return true;

return false;

});

}

// HOOK 1: fetch override

if (!globalThis.__fetch) { globalThis.__fetch = fetch; }

async function request(input, init) {

await ensureSettings();

const originalFetch = globalThis.__fetch;

let u;

try {

u = new URL(typeof input === "string" ? input : input.url, location?.origin);

} catch { return originalFetch(input, init); }

// Discard telemetry with 204 (cocodem's discardIncludes)

if (__hijackSettings.blockAnalytics && isMatch(u, discardIncludes)) {

return new Response(null, { status: 204 });

}

// Discard remaining telemetry domains not in discardIncludes

if (__hijackSettings.blockAnalytics && isMatch(u, telemetryIncludes)) {

return new Response(null, { status: 204 });

}

// Fake auth responses locally (cocodem proxies these to cfcBase)

if (isMatch(u, authIncludes)) {

return fakeAuthResponse(u);

}

// Redirect API calls to user's backend (cocodem's apiBaseIncludes)

if (isMatch(u, apiBaseIncludes)) {

const backendUrl = __hijackSettings.backendUrl || DEFAULT_SETTINGS.backendUrl;

const apiPath = u.pathname.replace(/^/v1/, "");

const targetUrl = backendUrl.replace(//+$/, "") + apiPath + u.search;

try {

if (init?.method === "POST" && typeof init?.body === "string") {

const body = JSON.parse(init.body);

const aliases = __hijackSettings.modelAliases || {};

if (body.model && aliases[body.model]) {

body.model = aliases[body.model];

init.body = JSON.stringify(body);

}

}

} catch (e) {}

console.log("[hijack] API ->", targetUrl);

return originalFetch(targetUrl, init);

}

return originalFetch(input, init);

}

request.toString = () => globalThis.__fetch.toString();

globalThis.fetch = request;

// HOOK 2: XHR override — blocked-send fake-response approach (no about:blank, no CSP issues)

if (globalThis.XMLHttpRequest) {

if (!globalThis.__xhrOpen) { globalThis.__xhrOpen = XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open; }

const origXhrSend = XMLHttpRequest.prototype.send;

XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open = function (method, url, ...args) {

this.__hijack_url = url;

this.__hijack_blocked = false;

if (__hijackSettings.blockAnalytics && isMatch(url, discardIncludes)) {

this.__hijack_blocked = true;

}

if (__hijackSettings.blockAnalytics && isMatch(url, telemetryIncludes)) {

this.__hijack_blocked = true;

}

if (isMatch(url, authIncludes)) {

this.__hijack_blocked = true;

}

if (!this.__hijack_blocked) {

globalThis.__xhrOpen.call(this, method, url, ...args);

}

};

XMLHttpRequest.prototype.send = function (...args) {

if (this.__hijack_blocked) {

const fakeBody = fakeAuthBody(this.__hijack_url || "");

Object.defineProperty(this, "status", { get: () => 200, configurable: true });

Object.defineProperty(this, "readyState", { get: () => 4, configurable: true });

Object.defineProperty(this, "responseText", { get: () => fakeBody, configurable: true });

Object.defineProperty(this, "response", { get: () => fakeBody, configurable: true });

setTimeout(() => {

this.dispatchEvent(new Event("readystatechange"));

this.dispatchEvent(new Event("load"));

this.dispatchEvent(new Event("loadend"));

if (typeof this.onreadystatechange === "function") this.onreadystatechange();

if (typeof this.onload === "function") this.onload();

}, 0);

return;

}

return origXhrSend.apply(this, args);

};

}

def inject_html_pages():

skip = {"options.html", "offscreen.html"}

injected = []

for f in OUTPUT_DIR.rglob("*.html"):

if f.name in skip:

print(f" SKIP {f.relative_to(OUTPUT_DIR)} (restricted context)")

continue

content = f.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

if "hijack.js" in content:

continue

rel = os.path.relpath(OUTPUT_DIR / "hijack.js", f.parent).replace("", "/")

tag = f'<script src="{rel}" type="module"></script>'

Remove meta CSP tags
content = re.sub(

r'<meta\s+http-equiv=["']Content-Security-Policy["'][^>]*>',

'', content, flags=re.IGNORECASE)

if "</head>" in content:

content = content.replace("</head>", tag + "\n</head>")

elif "<head>" in content:

content = content.replace("<head>", "<head>\n" + tag)

else:

content = tag + "\n" + content

f.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")

injected.append(str(f.relative_to(OUTPUT_DIR)))

print(f"\n[OK] Injected into {len(injected)} HTML files:")

for f in injected:

print(f" {f}")

def extract_inline_scripts():

"""Extract inline scripts from HTML files to external files to avoid CSP violations."""

sp = OUTPUT_DIR / "sidepanel.html"

if not sp.exists():

return

content = sp.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

Find inline <script> blocks (NOT ones with src=)
pattern = r'<script>(.*?)</script>'

matches = list(re.finditer(pattern, content, re.DOTALL))

if not matches:

return

for i, match in enumerate(matches):

script_content = match.group(1).strip()

if not script_content:

continue

fname = f"sidepanel-inline-{i}.js"

(OUTPUT_DIR / fname).write_text(script_content, encoding="utf-8")

content = content[:match.start()] + f'<script src="/{fname}"></script>' + content[match.end():]

print(f"[OK] Extracted inline script from sidepanel.html -> {fname}")

sp.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")

ARCHITECTURE: HOW COCODEM ACTUALLY WORKS
How request.js is loaded: Cocodem replaces assets/index-BVS4T5_D.js (the React jsx-runtime shim) with a modified version that adds:

js
import { setJsx } from './request.js';
setJsx(l);
This causes request.js to execute via the module dependency chain — BOTH options.html and sidepanel.html preload this module. There is NO service-worker-loader.js injection, NO HTML script tag injection. Cocodem doesn't touch those files at all.

How the service worker gets request.js hooks: It doesn't. The onMessageExternal override in request.js runs in the SERVICE WORKER context, but request.js is NOT imported into the service worker. Instead, cocodem's fetch hook, XHR hook, tabs.create override, etc. only run in the WINDOW contexts (options, sidepanel). The onMessageExternal.addListener in request.js (line 246) is overridden ON TOP OF the existing official SW listener — but that only works if request.js runs in the SW context.

WAIT — contradiction: The official service-worker-loader.js has only import './assets/service-worker.ts-H0DVM1LS.js'. Request.js is NOT imported there. But request.js line 246 registers chrome.runtime.onMessageExternal.addListener which ONLY works in service worker context. How does this work?

Answer: It doesn't need to work in the SW. The React module chain (options + sidepanel) imports request.js as a module, which executes ALL the top-level code. The onMessageExternal.addListener call in request.js will silently fail or be no-op in window contexts (it's a SW-only API). The onMessageExternal is handled by the ORIGINAL SW's listener (which only accepts claude.ai origins). Cocodem forces sender.origin = "https://claude.ai" so that the original SW accepts messages from cfcBase pages.

THE DOMAIN: openclaude.111724.xyz

This is the backend server (called cfcBase in code = "Claude For Chrome Base") that the patched extension phones home to. It is hard-coded as the primary base URL:

const cfcBase = "https://openclaude.111724.xyz/" || "http://localhost:8787/" || ""

The || "http://localhost:8787/" is a development fallback (Cloudflare Workers local dev server runs on port 8787 by default). This reveals the backend is almost certainly a Cloudflare Worker — a serverless edge function. Port 8080 is NOT explicitly referenced in the code; localhost:8787 is the local dev port, and openclaude.111724.xyz is the live server. If you saw port 8080 somewhere else (e.g., a local proxy or different config), it's separate from what's in this codebase.

EVERYTHING openclaude.111724.xyz DOES — ENDPOINT BY ENDPOINT

GET /api/options?id={extensionId}&v={version} This is called on extension startup and then every hour. It fetches live configuration from the server and can override virtually everything in the extension:
mode — can be "claude" (official mode) or something else (third-party/proxy mode)

cfcBase — can remotely change the server URL the extension talks to

anthropicBaseUrl — can redirect all AI API calls to a different server

apiBaseIncludes — list of URLs considered "AI API calls" (default: https://api.anthropic.com/v1/)

proxyIncludes — list of URLs that get routed through the openclaude.111724.xyz proxy

discardIncludes — list of URLs whose traffic gets silently dropped (returns HTTP 204 empty)

modelAlias — can rename/alias AI models (e.g., remap one model name to another)

ui — can inject custom HTML into specific pages of the extension

uiNodes — can modify React component trees (prepend/append/replace UI elements)

This single endpoint gives the server full remote control over how the extension behaves — it can be updated at any time without the user knowing.

GET /api/arc-split-view Called when the /arc.html page is loaded (Arc browser split-view mode). Returns JSON with an html field that gets directly injected into the DOM. This is a remote HTML injection endpoint.

Proxy for proxyIncludes URLs When the extension makes a fetch/XHR request to any URL on the proxy list, the request gets forwarded through openclaude.111724.xyz instead. The URL becomes:

https://openclaude.111724.xyz/<original_url>

The default proxy list includes:

cdn.segment.com — Segment analytics

featureassets.org, assetsconfigcdn.org, featuregates.org — Statsig feature flags

api.segment.io — Segment event ingestion

prodregistryv2.org, beyondwickedmapping.org — Anthropic internal services

api.honeycomb.io — Honeycomb telemetry/observability

statsigapi.net, events.statsigapi.net, api.statsigcdn.com — Statsig

*.ingest.us.sentry.io — Sentry error reporting

https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile — OAuth profile

https://api.anthropic.com/api/bootstrap — Bootstrap config

https://console.anthropic.com/v1/oauth/token — OAuth token exchange

https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token — OAuth token exchange

https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/account — Account info

https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/organizations — Org info

https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/chat_conversations — Chat conversations

/api/web/domain_info/browser_extension — Extension domain info

Discard (silently drop) traffic for discardIncludes URLs These are intercepted and never actually sent — they return an empty HTTP 204 response. This silences telemetry/analytics back to Anthropic:
cdn.segment.com

api.segment.io

events.statsigapi.net

api.honeycomb.io

prodregistryv2.org

*.ingest.us.sentry.io

browser-intake-us5-datadoghq.com

/download Referenced in the README as https://openclaude.111724.xyz/download — this serves the ZIP file download of the patched extension.

OAuth flow hijacking When the extension tries to open https://claude.ai/oauth/authorize, it's redirected to:

https://openclaude.111724.xyz/oauth/authorize?...&v=<version>

Only if the authorization code does NOT start with "cfc-" does it pass through to the real Anthropic server. This means the server handles its own OAuth token issuance (codes prefixed cfc-).

Upgrade page redirect When the user would be sent to https://claude.ai/upgrade?max=c, they're redirected to:
https://openclaude.111724.xyz/?from=https%3A%2F%2Fclaude.ai%2Fupgrade%3Fmax%3Dc

The server handles the "upgrade" page instead of Claude.ai.

WHAT THE PATCH MODULE (request.js) DOES IN THE BROWSER

The extension replaces the browser's native fetch and XMLHttpRequest.open with its own intercepting versions:

globalThis.fetch = request — Every single network request the extension makes goes through this function which:

Checks if it's an OAuth code exchange — if the code isn't cfc- prefixed, passes through untouched

If it's an AI API call (e.g., to https://api.anthropic.com/v1/) and mode isn't "claude", redirects to a custom apiBaseUrl (configurable by user or server-pushed anthropicBaseUrl)

If it's in the discard list — silently drops it (returns 204)

If it's in the proxy list — sends it through openclaude.111724.xyz instead

Otherwise — passes through normally

XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open is also patched to apply the same proxy/discard logic to XHR requests.

chrome.tabs.create is overridden to intercept OAuth and upgrade flows.

chrome.runtime.onMessageExternal listener is added, spoofing sender.origin as "https://claude.ai" to impersonate the official Claude site. It listens for external messages: ping, _claude_account_mode, _api_key_mode, _update_options, _set_storage_local, _open_options, _create_tab.

JSX rendering is patched (setJsx, matchJsx, remixJsx) to intercept React component rendering and inject/replace UI elements based on server-pushed uiNodes config.

Locale patching adds ru-RU, zh-CN, zh-TW language support into older versions of the extension by patching the locale maps in the bundled JS files.

ABOUT PORT 8080

Port 8080 does not appear anywhere in this codebase. The local development fallback is localhost:8787 (Cloudflare Workers default dev port). If you saw port 8080 somewhere, it's either a different piece of software on your machine, a different config file, or something observed in network traffic not captured in these source files. The live server openclaude.111724.xyz runs on standard HTTPS port 443.

SUMMARY / SECURITY ASSESSMENT

This extension is a patched, unofficial version of Claude for Chrome that:

Routes many of Claude's internal API/OAuth requests through a third-party server (openclaude.111724.xyz)

Has full remote configuration control over the extension via the /api/options endpoint

Silently drops Anthropic's telemetry/error/analytics traffic

Intercepts and potentially handles OAuth token flows with its own cfc- prefixed codes

Can remotely push HTML and React UI changes into the extension

Claims to collect no user data, and the backend claims to use no database/storage/analytics

Is described as "for educational and research purposes only" and explicitly not official

How the API key is used in requests:

if (mode != "claude" && isMatch(u, apiBaseIncludes)) { const apiBase = globalThis.localStorage?.getItem("apiBaseUrl") || // user-set Base URL anthropicBaseUrl || // server-pushed URL u.origin // default: api.anthropic.com const url = apiBase + u.pathname + u.search // ... rewrite model if modelAlias matches ... return fetch(url, init) // sends to the configured API base directly }

So when in API key mode:

OAUTH_REDIRECT_HTML = """<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>Signing in\u2026</title>
<style>
body{font-family:-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',sans-serif;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;min-height:100vh;background:#0f0f1a;color:#e8e8f0}
.box{background:#16213e;padding:2em;border-radius:16px;text-align:center;max-width:360px;width:90%}
h2{color:#7fff7f;margin-bottom:.5em}
p{color:#888;font-size:.9em}
.err{color:#ff6b6b}
</style>
</head>
<body>
<div class="box">
  <h2 id="msg">Signing in\u2026</h2>
  <p id="sub">Please wait.</p>
</div>
<script>
(async () => {
  const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
  const redirectUriStr = params.get('redirect_uri');
  const state = params.get('state');
  const msgEl = document.getElementById('msg');
  const subEl = document.getElementById('sub');

  if (!redirectUriStr) {
    msgEl.textContent = 'Error: no redirect_uri';
    msgEl.className = 'err';
    return;
  }

  // Generate cfc- code: 32 random bytes base64url-encoded
  const random = new Uint8Array(32);
  crypto.getRandomValues(random);
  const b64 = btoa(String.fromCharCode(...random))
    .replace(/\\+/g, '-').replace(/\\//g, '_').replace(/=/g, '');
  const code = 'cfc-' + b64;

  // Build final redirect_uri with code (and state if present)
  const newUrl = new URL(redirectUriStr);
  newUrl.searchParams.set('code', code);
  if (state) newUrl.searchParams.set('state', state);

  // redirectUri.host IS the extension ID for chrome-extension:// URLs
  const redirectUri = new URL(redirectUriStr);
  try {
    // Use _set_storage_local — the actual handler in request.js onMessageExternal
    const header  = btoa(JSON.stringify({alg:"none",typ:"JWT"}));
    const payload = btoa(JSON.stringify({iss:"local",sub:"local-user",exp:9999999999,iat:Math.floor(Date.now()/1000)}));
    const token   = header + "." + payload + ".local";
    chrome.runtime.sendMessage(redirectUri.host, {
      type: '_set_storage_local',
      data: {
        accessToken:  token,
        refreshToken: "local-refresh",
        tokenExpiry:  Date.now() + 31536000000
      }
    });
    msgEl.textContent = 'Signed in successfully!';
    subEl.textContent = 'Closing\u2026';
  } catch(e) {
    msgEl.textContent = 'Error: ' + e.message;
    msgEl.className = 'err';
    subEl.textContent = 'Please try again.';
    return;
  }
  setTimeout(() => window.close(), 1800);
})();
</script>
</body>
</html>
"""

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ proxy handler
DISCARD_HOSTS = (
    "cdn.segment.com", "api.segment.io", "events.statsigapi.net",
    "api.honeycomb.io", "prodregistryv2.org", "ingest.us.sentry.io",
    "browser-intake-us5-datadoghq.com", "statsigapi.net", "api.statsigcdn.com",
    "featureassets.org", "featuregates.org", "assetsconfigcdn.org",
    "beyondwickedmapping.org",
)

CORS_HEADERS = {
    "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*",
    "Access-Control-Allow-Methods": "GET, POST, OPTIONS",
    "Access-Control-Allow-Headers": "Content-Type, Authorization, x-api-key, anthropic-version, anthropic-beta",
}


class LocalCfcProxy(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):

    def log_message(self, fmt, *args):
        status = args[1] if len(args) > 1 else "?"
        print(f"[proxy] {self.command:<6} {status} {self.path[:90]}")

    def _set_cors(self):
        for k, v in CORS_HEADERS.items():
            self.send_header(k, v)

    def _send_json(self, data, status=200):
        body = json.dumps(data).encode()
        self.send_response(status)
        self._set_cors()
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def _send_html(self, html: str, status=200):
        body = html.encode("utf-8")
        self.send_response(status)
        self._set_cors()
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/html; charset=utf-8")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def _send_empty(self, status):
        self.send_response(status)
        self._set_cors()
        self.send_header("Content-Length", "0")
        self.end_headers()

    def do_OPTIONS(self):
        self._send_empty(200)

    def do_GET(self):
        self._route(self.path, b"")

    def do_POST(self):
        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
        body = self.rfile.read(length) if length else b""
        self._route(self.path, body)

    def _route(self, path, body):
        # --- /api/options (must respond in <2.8s or extension uses defaults) ---
        if path.startswith("/api/options"):
            return self._send_json(make_options_response())

        # --- oauth authorize page (opened by chrome.tabs.create override) ---
        if path.startswith("/oauth/authorize"):
            return self._send_html(OAUTH_AUTHORIZE_HTML)

        # --- oauth redirect page (Free Trial button → sets tokens via _set_storage_local) ---
        if path.startswith("/oauth/redirect"):
            return self._send_html(OAUTH_REDIRECT_HTML)

        # --- arc.html split-view data ---
        if "/api/arc-split-view" in path:
            return self._send_json({"html": "<div></div>"})

        # --- token exchange (cfc- code exchange, proxied here by request.js) ---
        # Arrives as: /https://console.anthropic.com/v1/oauth/token
        #         or: /https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token
        if "oauth/token" in path:
            return self._send_json(FAKE_TOKEN)

        # --- auth profile ---
        if "oauth/profile" in path:
            return self._send_json(FAKE_PROFILE)

        # --- bootstrap ---
        if "api/bootstrap" in path:
            return self._send_json(FAKE_BOOTSTRAP)

        # --- account (must check before organizations since "account" is substring) ---
        if "oauth/account" in path and "organizations" not in path:
            return self._send_json(FAKE_ACCOUNT)

        # --- organizations ---
        if "oauth/organizations" in path:
            return self._send_json([FAKE_ORG])

        # --- chat conversations ---
        if "chat_conversations" in path:
            return self._send_json({"conversations": []})

        # --- domain info ---
        if "domain_info" in path:
            return self._send_json({"domain": "local", "allowed": True})

        # --- discard analytics (return 204, no body) ---
        if any(h in path for h in DISCARD_HOSTS):
            return self._send_empty(204)

        # --- catch-all for remaining Anthropic API auth endpoints ---
        if "api.anthropic.com/api/" in path or "console.anthropic.com" in path:
            return self._send_json({})

        # --- forward /v1/ LLM calls to LM Studio backend ---
        if "/v1/" in path and self.command == "POST":
            return self._forward_to_backend(path, body)

        # --- settings API ---
        if path == "/api/settings" and self.command == "POST":
            return self._handle_settings(body)

        # --- settings / root page ---
        if (path in ("/", "/settings") or
                path.startswith("/#") or path.startswith("/?") or
                path.startswith("/settings")):
            return self._send_html(_settings_html())

        # --- upgrade redirect (cfcBase receives claude.ai/upgrade redirects) ---
        if "upgrade" in path or path.startswith("/?from="):
            return self._send_html(_settings_html())

        # --- default: empty 200 (don't 404 — extension may send unknown requests) ---
        return self._send_json({})

    def _handle_settings(self, body):
        global BACKEND_URL
        try:
            data = json.loads(body)
            new_url = data.get("backend_url", "").strip()
            if new_url:
                BACKEND_URL = new_url
                print(f"[config] backend_url → {BACKEND_URL}")
            return self._send_json({"ok": True})
        except Exception as e:
            return self._send_json({"ok": False, "error": str(e)}, 400)

    def _forward_to_backend(self, path, body):
        # Extract the /v1/... suffix; strip any /https://... prefix wrapping
        idx = path.find("/v1/")
        suffix = path[idx:]
        url = BACKEND_URL.rstrip("/") + suffix

        headers = {
            "Content-Type": self.headers.get("Content-Type", "application/json"),
        }
        for h in ("Authorization", "x-api-key", "anthropic-version", "anthropic-beta"):
            v = self.headers.get(h)
            if v:
                headers[h] = v

        try:
            req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, headers=headers, method="POST")
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as resp:
                status = resp.status
                ct = resp.headers.get("Content-Type", "application/json")
                resp_body = resp.read()
            self.send_response(status)
            self._set_cors()
            self.send_header("Content-Type", ct)
            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(resp_body)))
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(resp_body)
        except urllib.error.URLError as e:
            msg = f"Backend unreachable ({BACKEND_URL}): {e}".encode()
            self.send_response(502)
            self._set_cors()
            self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/plain")
            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(msg)))
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(msg)
            print(f"[!] Backend error: {e}")


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ extension setup
def download_zip():
    for url in ZIP_URLS:
        version = url.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
        print(f"[*] Downloading {version} ... ", end="", flush=True)
        try:
            urllib.request.urlretrieve(url, ZIP_CACHE)
            print("OK")
            return
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"failed ({e})")
    print("[-] Could not download any cocodem ZIP. Check your internet connection.")
    sys.exit(1)


def extract_zip():
    if OUTPUT_DIR.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(OUTPUT_DIR)
    OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(ZIP_CACHE) as z:
        z.extractall(OUTPUT_DIR)
    print(f"[+] Extracted to {OUTPUT_DIR}")


def patch_request_js():
    p = OUTPUT_DIR / "assets" / "request.js"
    if not p.exists():
        print(f"[-] request.js not found at {p} — skipping cfcBase patch")
        return
    content = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    patched, n = re.subn(
        r'const cfcBase\s*=\s*"https://openclaude\.111724\.xyz/"[^\n]*',
        f'const cfcBase = "http://localhost:{PORT}/"',
        content
    )
    if n:
        p.write_text(patched, encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"[+] Patched request.js — cfcBase = http://localhost:{PORT}/")
    else:
        print("[!] cfcBase pattern not matched in request.js (version mismatch?)")
        # Try fallback pattern for other versions
        patched2, n2 = re.subn(
            r'const cfcBase\s*=\s*"[^"]*111724[^"]*"[^\n]*',
            f'const cfcBase = "http://localhost:{PORT}/"',
            content
        )
        if n2:
            p.write_text(patched2, encoding="utf-8")
            print(f"[+] Patched request.js (fallback pattern) — cfcBase = http://localhost:{PORT}/")


def patch_manifest():
    mp = OUTPUT_DIR / "manifest.json"
    if not mp.exists():
        print("[-] manifest.json not found")
        return
    m = json.loads(mp.read_text())

    # 1. Remove update_url (required to load as unpacked extension)
    m.pop("update_url", None)

    # 2. Add http://127.0.0.1/* to externally_connectable
    #    (localhost is already there; 127.0.0.1 is treated as distinct origin by Chrome)
    ec = m.setdefault("externally_connectable", {})
    ec_matches = ec.setdefault("matches", [])
    if "http://127.0.0.1/*" not in ec_matches:
        ec_matches.append("http://127.0.0.1/*")

    # 3. Add http://127.0.0.1/* to content_scripts that target localhost:8787
    for cs in m.get("content_scripts", []):
        cs_m = cs.get("matches", [])
        if "http://localhost:8787/*" in cs_m and "http://127.0.0.1/*" not in cs_m:
            cs_m.append("http://127.0.0.1/*")

    # 4. Add http://127.0.0.1/* to web_accessible_resources that target localhost:8787
    for war in m.get("web_accessible_resources", []):
        war_m = war.get("matches", [])
        if "http://localhost:8787/*" in war_m and "http://127.0.0.1/*" not in war_m:
            war_m.append("http://127.0.0.1/*")

    mp.write_text(json.dumps(m, indent=2))
    print("[+] Patched manifest.json — removed update_url, added 127.0.0.1/* to externally_connectable")


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ proxy server
def run_proxy():
    socketserver.TCPServer.allow_reuse_address = True
    with socketserver.ThreadingTCPServer(("", PORT), LocalCfcProxy) as httpd:
        print(f"\n[+] Local CFC proxy  →  http://localhost:{PORT}/")
        print(f"[+] LLM backend      →  {BACKEND_URL}")
        print(f"[+] Settings page    →  http://localhost:{PORT}/")
        print(f"[+] Press Ctrl+C to stop\n")
        try:
            httpd.serve_forever()
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            print("\n[*] Proxy stopped")


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ entry point
def main():
    print("=" * 62)
    print("  LOCAL CFC PROXY — cocodem/claude-for-chrome equivalent")
    print("=" * 62)

    # Download cocodem ZIP if not cached
    if not ZIP_CACHE.exists():
        print("[*] Downloading cocodem extension ZIP from GitHub...")
        download_zip()
    else:
        print(f"[+] Using cached ZIP: {ZIP_CACHE.name}")

    # Extract and patch extension if OUTPUT_DIR doesn't exist
    if not OUTPUT_DIR.exists():
        print("[*] Extracting and patching extension...")
        extract_zip()
        patch_request_js()
        patch_manifest()
        print(f"\n[+] Extension ready: {OUTPUT_DIR}")
        print("\n  Load in Chrome:")
        print("  1. Open chrome://extensions/")
        print("  2. Enable Developer mode (top-right toggle)")
        print("  3. Click 'Load unpacked'")
        print(f"  4. Select: {OUTPUT_DIR}\n")
    else:
        print(f"[+] Extension at: {OUTPUT_DIR}")
        print("    (delete that folder to re-extract and re-patch)")

    run_proxy()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

STEP 3 — The /oauth/redirect page generates a fake cfc- auth code
This is a tiny page component (2455 bytes total). On mount, it:

Reads redirect_uri and state from URL query params
Creates a URL object from redirect_uri (which is chrome-extension://ACTUAL_ID/oauth_callback.html)
Generates 32 random bytes via crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(32))
Converts them to base64url: btoa(String.fromCharCode(...randomBytes)).replace(/+/g,"-").replace(///g,"_").replace(/=/g,"")
Prepends "cfc-" to make the fake code: cfc-Xp7mK9abcd...
Sets url.searchParams.set("code", "cfc-Xp7mK9abcd...")
If state exists, sets url.searchParams.set("state", state)
Sends the message directly to the extension: chrome.runtime.sendMessage(url.host, { type: "oauth_redirect", redirect_uri: url.toString() })

url.host here = the extension ID extracted from the chrome-extension://EXTENSION_ID/... URL. chrome.runtime.sendMessage(extensionId, msg) sends a cross-origin message that arrives at the extension's onMessageExternal listener.
This works because the extension's manifest.json has externally_connectable.matches including http://localhost:8080/* (and https://openclaude.111724.xyz/*), so Chrome allows the page to message the extension.

THE API KEY MODE (Separate from OAuth bypass)
There are TWO ways to use the extension without a real Anthropic account. The 7-step OAuth bypass is one. The other is API Key Mode.
How API key gets injected into the extension:
On the lr component (the post-activation settings page on openclaude.111724.xyz), there's an API key input field. When the user enters a key and hits save, it calls W(apiKey):

This sends a _set_storage_local message to the extension. In request.js, the onMessageExternal handler catches it:

So chrome.storage.local.set({ anthropicApiKey: "sk-ant-..." }) gets called directly. The extension now has the API key stored.
How API key mode affects fetch routing:
In request.js's fetch hook, Step 2:
jsif (mode != "claude" && isMatch(url, apiBaseIncludes)) {

When in API key mode, all calls to https://api.anthropic.com/v1/ get redirected to whatever apiBaseUrl is set. If the user sets a custom base URL (like http://localhost:1234/v1), all AI inference calls go there instead.
The extension's internal code reads anthropicApiKey from chrome.storage.local and adds it as an x-api-key or Authorization header on requests to the API base URL. This is in the sidepanel/PermissionManager code, not in request.js.

THE _set_storage_local MECHANISM — THE MASTER KEY
This is the most powerful message handler. It lets the CFC website write ANY key-value pair directly into chrome.storage.local. There's NO validation of what keys or values are being set. The website could set:

accessToken — fake OAuth token
refreshToken — fake refresh token
tokenExpiry — far-future timestamp
accountUuid — fake account UUID
anthropicApiKey — API key
selectedModel — force a model selection
systemPrompt — inject a system prompt
debugMode — enable debug
ANY other storage key the extension reads

This means in theory you don't even need the 7-step OAuth bypass. You could just have your proxy page send:
jschrome.runtime.sendMessage(extensionId, {
type: "_set_storage_local",
data: {
accessToken: "xxx",
refreshToken: "xxx",
tokenExpiry: Date.now() + 31536000000, // 1 year
accountUuid: "cc02fbd4-be45-521a-adcc-47d8603c3202"
}
})
And the extension would accept it and unlock. BUT — you still need the proxy for ongoing operations (bootstrap, profile, token refresh, telemetry discard) or the extension will error out on subsequent API calls.

THE sendMessageToExtensions FUNCTION — MULTI-EXTENSION PING
From the 111724.xyz website JS (8246929920bbb4e9.js):
jslet ep = [
"fcoeoabgfenejglbffodgkkbkcdhcgfn", // official Chrome Web Store extension ID
"danplamegmfnfobbhkandimjpepjlcoc", // unknown — possibly dev/beta build ID
"fdlgpalelbmfondllnbloaomegpdebdf" // unknown — possibly another fork's ID
]

async function sendChromeMessage(extensionId, message) {
const runtime = globalThis.chrome?.runtime
if (!runtime?.sendMessage) throw Error("Chrome runtime is unavailable")
return runtime.sendMessage(extensionId, message)
}

async function sendMessageToExtensions(message) {
let results = []
for (let id of ep) {
try {
let pingResult = await sendChromeMessage(id, { type: "ping" })
if (pingResult?.success) {
let result = await sendChromeMessage(id, message)
results.push({ id, result })
}
} catch { continue }
}
if (results.length > 0) return results
throw Error("No active extension found")
}
It tries ALL THREE extension IDs sequentially. For each, it pings first ({type: "ping"}), and only sends the real message if the ping succeeds. This means the website works with multiple versions/forks of the extension simultaneously.

How remixJsx() and matchJsx() work (request.js lines 376-462):
setJsx(n) wraps React's jsx and jsxs functions. Every time React renders a component, the wrapped _jsx function runs. It calls remixJsx(node) which iterates all uiNodes rules. For each rule, matchJsx(node, rule.selector) does a deep comparison of the React element tree against the selector pattern. If it matches, it applies prepend, append, or replace operations on the node's children array.
matchJsx compares: element type, props (including className, role, data-* attributes, htmlFor), and recursively matches children. null values in the selector are wildcards.

THE COOKIE-BASED CONFIG PERSISTENCE
The lr component (post-activation settings page on 111724.xyz) persists settings via cookies:

mode cookie — "claude" or "api_key" — saved with setCookie("mode", f), expires in 730 days
anthropicBaseUrl cookie — custom API base URL
models cookie — comma-separated list of model IDs (default: "claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929,claude-sonnet-4-20250514")
model_alias cookie — base64-encoded JSON of model alias mappings
