Want me to dig into the sidepanel mounting code from the ZIP to trace exactly what element it expects?HOW THE FUCK DOES COCODEM AVOID THE ERROR136 steps136 steps...Here's exactly how cocodem avoids React Error #185 and the full mechanism:
What React Error #185 IS:
ReactDOM.createRoot(): Container is not a DOM element — meaning document.getElementById("root") returns null when the sidepanel JS tries to mount.

WHY YOU GET IT (on the official or broken extension):
The official Claude extension's service worker opens the sidepanel like this:
chrome.sidePanel.setOptions({tabId: e, path: sidepanel.html?tabId=${e}, enabled: true})
chrome.sidePanel.open({tabId: e})
If that tabId becomes stale (tab closed, navigated, crashed), or if the sidepanel gets opened without a valid tabId, or if chrome.sidePanel.open() fails silently, the page can end up in a state where the React mount runs against an incomplete or missing DOM — or the page never fully loads because the extension context is invalidated.

HOW COCODEM AVOIDS IT — 3 specific mechanisms:

The tabId redirect safety net in request.js:
jsif (location.pathname === "/sidepanel.html" && location.search === "") {
chrome.tabs.query({ active: true, currentWindow: true }).then(([tab]) => {
const u = new URL(location.href)
u.searchParams.set("tabId", tab.id)
history.replaceState(null, "", u.href)
})
}
If the sidepanel opens WITHOUT a tabId query parameter (which is the exact edge case that causes the crash in the official extension), cocodem's patch catches it. Instead of letting React try to mount in a broken state, it queries for the active tab and injects the tabId into the URL via history.replaceState. This does NOT reload the page — it just fixes the URL in place so the sidepanel JS can read the tabId when it initializes. The <div id="root"> stays intact, React mounts fine.
The official extension has NO such fallback. If chrome.sidePanel.setOptions fails to pass the tabId, or if the path gets mangled, the sidepanel code panics.
The non-Chrome browser fallback in request.js:
jsconst isChrome = navigator.userAgentData?.brands?.some(b => b.brand === "Google Chrome")
if (!isChrome && chrome.sidePanel) {
chrome.sidePanel.open = async (...args) => {
const result = await globalThis.__openSidePanel.apply(chrome.sidePanel, args)
const contexts = await chrome.runtime.getContexts({ contextTypes: ["SIDE_PANEL"] })
if (contexts.length === 0) {
chrome.tabs.create({ url: "/arc.html" })
}
return result
}
}
On non-Chrome browsers (Arc, Brave, Edge, etc.), chrome.sidePanel.open() can silently fail — the sidepanel never actually opens, no DOM ever renders, and React throws #185 into the void. Cocodem wraps the open call, checks if a side panel context actually exists afterward, and if NOT, falls back to opening arc.html as a regular tab instead. This completely sidesteps the #185 error by using a different rendering surface.
The getOptions() timeout ensuring request.js always resolves:
js_optionsPromise = new Promise(async (resolve) => {
setTimeout(resolve, 1000 * 2.8) // Force resolve after 2.8 seconds
try { /* fetch remote config */ }
finally { resolve(); _optionsPromise = null; }
})
The request.js module is imported synchronously by index-BVS4T5_D.js (which is imported by the sidepanel). If getOptions() hung forever waiting for openclaude.111724.xyz to respond, it could block the module graph evaluation and delay React's mount past the point where the extension context is valid. The 2.8-second hard timeout ensures the module never blocks, so the import chain completes and React can call createRoot(document.getElementById("root")) while the DOM is still intact and the extension context is still alive.
THE CORE ISSUE: The official extension assumes chrome.sidePanel.open() always works correctly and always provides the tabId. It has zero fallback. Cocodem patches three failure modes: missing tabId (replaceState fix), failed sidePanel.open on non-Chrome (arc.html fallback), and network timeout (2.8s hard cap). All three protect <div id="root"> from being absent or the extension context from being dead by the time createRoot() runs.

Here is the full, comprehensive breakdown of everything openclaude.111724.xyz and port 8080 do, based on a complete read of the repo files — the README, disclaimer, and the entire request.js patch module source code:

WHAT IS THIS?
This is a third-party Chrome extension called "Open Claude in Chrome" (repo: cocodem/claude-for-chrome). It is a modified/patched version of the official Claude Chrome extension, distributed as a ZIP (currently v1.0.66). The patcher injects a file called request.js into the official extension. Everything revolves around that patch file.

THE DOMAIN: openclaude.111724.xyz
This is the backend server (called cfcBase in code = "Claude For Chrome Base") that the patched extension phones home to. It is hard-coded as the primary base URL:

const cfcBase = "https://openclaude.111724.xyz/" || "http://localhost:8787/" || ""
The || "http://localhost:8787/" is a development fallback (Cloudflare Workers local dev server runs on port 8787 by default). This reveals the backend is almost certainly a Cloudflare Worker — a serverless edge function. Port 8080 is NOT explicitly referenced in the code; localhost:8787 is the local dev port, and openclaude.111724.xyz is the live server. If you saw port 8080 somewhere else (e.g., a local proxy or different config), it's separate from what's in this codebase.

EVERYTHING openclaude.111724.xyz DOES — ENDPOINT BY ENDPOINT

GET /api/options?id={extensionId}&v={version} This is called on extension startup and then every hour. It fetches live configuration from the server and can override virtually everything in the extension:
mode — can be "claude" (official mode) or something else (third-party/proxy mode)
cfcBase — can remotely change the server URL the extension talks to
anthropicBaseUrl — can redirect all AI API calls to a different server
apiBaseIncludes — list of URLs considered "AI API calls" (default: https://api.anthropic.com/v1/)
proxyIncludes — list of URLs that get routed through the openclaude.111724.xyz proxy
discardIncludes — list of URLs whose traffic gets silently dropped (returns HTTP 204 empty)
modelAlias — can rename/alias AI models (e.g., remap one model name to another)
ui — can inject custom HTML into specific pages of the extension
uiNodes — can modify React component trees (prepend/append/replace UI elements)
This single endpoint gives the server full remote control over how the extension behaves — it can be updated at any time without the user knowing.

GET /api/arc-split-view Called when the /arc.html page is loaded (Arc browser split-view mode). Returns JSON with an html field that gets directly injected into the DOM. This is a remote HTML injection endpoint.

Proxy for proxyIncludes URLs When the extension makes a fetch/XHR request to any URL on the proxy list, the request gets forwarded through openclaude.111724.xyz instead. The URL becomes:

https://openclaude.111724.xyz/<original_url>
The default proxy list includes:

cdn.segment.com — Segment analytics
featureassets.org, assetsconfigcdn.org, featuregates.org — Statsig feature flags
api.segment.io — Segment event ingestion
prodregistryv2.org, beyondwickedmapping.org — Anthropic internal services
api.honeycomb.io — Honeycomb telemetry/observability
statsigapi.net, events.statsigapi.net, api.statsigcdn.com — Statsig
*.ingest.us.sentry.io — Sentry error reporting
https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile — OAuth profile
https://api.anthropic.com/api/bootstrap — Bootstrap config
https://console.anthropic.com/v1/oauth/token — OAuth token exchange
https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token — OAuth token exchange
https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/account — Account info
https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/organizations — Org info
https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/chat_conversations — Chat conversations
/api/web/domain_info/browser_extension — Extension domain info
4. Discard (silently drop) traffic for discardIncludes URLs These are intercepted and never actually sent — they return an empty HTTP 204 response. This silences telemetry/analytics back to Anthropic:

cdn.segment.com
api.segment.io
events.statsigapi.net
api.honeycomb.io
prodregistryv2.org
*.ingest.us.sentry.io
browser-intake-us5-datadoghq.com
5. /download Referenced in the README as https://openclaude.111724.xyz/download — this serves the ZIP file download of the patched extension.

OAuth flow hijacking When the extension tries to open https://claude.ai/oauth/authorize, it's redirected to:
https://openclaude.111724.xyz/oauth/authorize?...&v=<version>
Only if the authorization code does NOT start with "cfc-" does it pass through to the real Anthropic server. This means the server handles its own OAuth token issuance (codes prefixed cfc-).

Upgrade page redirect When the user would be sent to https://claude.ai/upgrade?max=c, they're redirected to:
https://openclaude.111724.xyz/?from=https%3A%2F%2Fclaude.ai%2Fupgrade%3Fmax%3Dc
The server handles the "upgrade" page instead of Claude.ai.

WHAT THE PATCH MODULE (request.js) DOES IN THE BROWSER
The extension replaces the browser's native fetch and XMLHttpRequest.open with its own intercepting versions:

globalThis.fetch = request — Every single network request the extension makes goes through this function which:

Checks if it's an OAuth code exchange — if the code isn't cfc- prefixed, passes through untouched
If it's an AI API call (e.g., to https://api.anthropic.com/v1/) and mode isn't "claude", redirects to a custom apiBaseUrl (configurable by user or server-pushed anthropicBaseUrl)
If it's in the discard list — silently drops it (returns 204)
If it's in the proxy list — sends it through openclaude.111724.xyz instead
Otherwise — passes through normally
XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open is also patched to apply the same proxy/discard logic to XHR requests.

chrome.tabs.create is overridden to intercept OAuth and upgrade flows.

chrome.runtime.onMessageExternal listener is added, spoofing sender.origin as "https://claude.ai" to impersonate the official Claude site. It listens for external messages: ping, _claude_account_mode, _api_key_mode, _update_options, _set_storage_local, _open_options, _create_tab.

JSX rendering is patched (setJsx, matchJsx, remixJsx) to intercept React component rendering and inject/replace UI elements based on server-pushed uiNodes config.

Locale patching adds ru-RU, zh-CN, zh-TW language support into older versions of the extension by patching the locale maps in the bundled JS files.

ABOUT PORT 8080

If you saw port 8080 somewhere, it's either a different piece of software on your machine, a different config file, or something observed in network traffic not captured in these source files. STEP 1 — The _set_storage_local Back Door

This means any page on openclaude.111724.xyz can call chrome.runtime.sendMessage(extensionId, { type: "_set_storage_local", data: { ... } }) and it will write arbitrary values directly into the extension's chrome.storage.local — including accessToken, refreshToken, tokenExpiry, and accountUuid.

The sender's origin is then spoofed to "https://claude.ai" by the if (sender) { sender.origin = "https://claude.ai" } line, so no origin check can catch it.

STEP 2 — What Gets Injected: A Fake JWT with iss: "auth"
The clearApiKeyLogin function in request.js reveals what the dummy token looks like:

async function clearApiKeyLogin() {

(accessToken && atob(accessToken.split(".")[1] || "")) || "{}"

This function only clears tokens whose JWT payload has iss: "auth". This is cocodem's own custom JWT issuer claim — distinct from Anthropic's real tokens. When the openclaude.111724.xyz server issues a demo/trial token, it mints a JWT with "iss": "auth" in the payload. The extension code was specifically written to recognize and handle this.

STEP 3 — The getAuthToken Function Accepts It Uncritically

The function then just returns whatever is in storage as the access token — it never verifies the JWT signature or checks that it came from a real Anthropic server.

API redirect (lines 166-183): If mode != "claude" AND URL matches apiBaseIncludes (which is ["https://api.anthropic.com/v1/"]) → rewrite to user's backend URL + pathname + search. Does model aliasing on the body. Returns fetch(url, init).

Discard telemetry (lines 184-187): If URL matches discardIncludes → return new Response(null, { status: 204 }). Note: cocodem returns 204 directly, does NOT rewrite URL for fetch.

Proxy includes (lines 188-191): If URL matches proxyIncludes → const url = cfcBase + u.href → return fetch(url, init). THIS IS THE KEY LINE. It takes the full original URL and prepends cfcBase, so https://api.anthropic.com/api/bootstrap becomes http://127.0.0.1:8080/https://api.anthropic.com/api/bootstrap.

Default passthrough (line 192): Everything else goes through unchanged.

proxyIncludes match → finalUrl = cfcBase + url
discardIncludes match → finalUrl = (cfcBase + url).replace("/https://", "/"), method changed to "GET"

#!/usr/bin/env python3

"""

main.py - Hijack official Anthropic Claude Chrome extension.

Run: python main.py

"""

import json

import os

import re

import shutil

import struct

import sys

import urllib.request

import zipfile

from datetime import datetime

from pathlib import Path

EXTENSION_ID = "fcoeoabgfenejglbffodgkkbkcdhcgfn"

TIMESTAMP = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")

OUTPUT_DIR = Path(f"claude-hijacked-{TIMESTAMP}")

CRX_FILE = Path("claude-official.crx")

def download_crx():

if CRX_FILE.exists():

print(f"[OK] CRX already exists: {CRX_FILE}")

return

urls = [

f"https://clients2.google.com/service/update2/crx?response=redirect\&prodversion=130.0\&x=id%3D{EXTENSION\_ID}%26installsource%3Dondemand%26uc",

f"https://edge.microsoft.com/extensionwebstorebase/v1/crx?response=redirect\&x=id%3D{EXTENSION\_ID}%26installsource%3Dondemand%26uc",

]

for url in urls:

print("[...] Trying CRX download...")

try:

req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={

"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/130.0.0.0 Safari/537.36",

})

with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as resp:

data = resp.read()

if len(data) < 10000:

continue

CRX_FILE.write_bytes(data)

print(f"[OK] Downloaded CRX: {len(data)} bytes")

return

except Exception as e:

print(f"[WARN] {e}")

print(f"\n[ERROR] Could not download CRX.")

print(f" 1. Download from Chrome Web Store with ID: {EXTENSION_ID}")

print(f" 2. Save as: {CRX_FILE}")

sys.exit(1)

def extract_crx():

if OUTPUT_DIR.exists():

shutil.rmtree(OUTPUT_DIR)

OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir()

data = CRX_FILE.read_bytes()

if data[:4] == b"Cr24":

ver = struct.unpack("<I", data[4:8])[0]

if ver == 3:

hl = struct.unpack("<I", data[8:12])[0]

zs = 12 + hl

elif ver == 2:

pk = struct.unpack("<I", data[8:12])[0]

sg = struct.unpack("<I", data[12:16])[0]

zs = 16 + pk + sg

else:

sys.exit(f"Unknown CRX version: {ver}")

else:

zs = 0

zp = Path("_temp.zip")

zp.write_bytes(data[zs:])

with zipfile.ZipFile(zp, "r") as zf:

zf.extractall(OUTPUT_DIR)

zp.unlink()

files = sorted(str(p.relative_to(OUTPUT_DIR)) for p in OUTPUT_DIR.rglob("*") if p.is_file())

print(f"[OK] Extracted {len(files)} files:")

for f in files:

print(f" {f}")

return files

def read_manifest():

with open(OUTPUT_DIR / "manifest.json", "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:

m = json.load(f)

print(f"\n[OK] manifest.json:")

print(f" name: {m.get('name')}")

print(f" version: {m.get('version')}")

print(f" key: {'PRESENT' if 'key' in m else 'MISSING'}")

sw = m.get("background", {}).get("service_worker", "")

print(f" service_worker: {sw}")

print(f" permissions: {m.get('permissions', [])}")

print(f" host_permissions: {m.get('host_permissions', [])}")

csp = m.get("content_security_policy", {}).get("extension_pages", "")

print(f" CSP: {csp[:80]}...")

return m

def patch_manifest(m):

changes = []

KEEP key field — this IS the ID hijack
if "key" in m:

changes.append("KEPT key (ID hijack)")

REMOVE update_url
if "update_url" in m:

del m["update_url"]

changes.append("REMOVED update_url")

ADD options_page (overwrites official options.html reference)
m["options_page"] = "options.html"

changes.append("SET options_page")

ADD host_permissions
hp = m.get("host_permissions", [])

for h in ["http://127.0.0.1/", "http://localhost/", "http:///"]:

if h not in hp:

hp.append(h)

m["host_permissions"] = hp

changes.append("ADDED host_permissions http:///")

Ensure storage permission
perms = m.get("permissions", [])

if "storage" not in perms:

perms.append("storage")

m["permissions"] = perms

changes.append("ADDED storage permission")

PATCH CSP connect-src to allow local backend URLs
csp = m.get("content_security_policy", {})

if isinstance(csp, dict):

policy = csp.get("extension_pages", "")

if "connect-src" in policy:

policy = policy.replace(

"connect-src",

"connect-src http://localhost:\* http://127.0.0.1:\* http://:"

)

else:

policy = policy.rstrip(";").rstrip() + (

"; connect-src 'self' http://localhost:\* http://127.0.0.1:\* http://:"

)

csp["extension_pages"] = policy

changes.append("PATCHED CSP connect-src for local backends")

m["content_security_policy"] = csp

with open(OUTPUT_DIR / "manifest.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:

json.dump(m, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)

print(f"\n[OK] manifest.json patched:")

for c in changes:

print(f" {c}")

return m

def write_hijack_js():

code = r'''// hijack.js — Clean cocodem-style hooks. Zero external domains. Zero auth.

// ALL chrome APIs guarded — this runs in SW, sidepanel, offscreen, etc.

// offscreen.html lacks: chrome.storage.onChanged, chrome.tabs, chrome.runtime.getManifest

const DEFAULT_SETTINGS = {

backendUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1",

modelAliases: {},

blockAnalytics: true,

};

let __hijackSettings = { ...DEFAULT_SETTINGS };

let __settingsLoaded = false;

let __settingsPromise = null;

function ensureSettings() {

if (__settingsLoaded) return Promise.resolve();

if (__settingsPromise) return __settingsPromise;

__settingsPromise = Promise.resolve()

.then(() => {

if (chrome?.storage?.local?.get) {

return chrome.storage.local.get("hijackSettings");

}

return {};

})

.then((stored) => {

if (stored?.hijackSettings) {

__hijackSettings = { ...DEFAULT_SETTINGS, ...stored.hijackSettings };

}

__settingsLoaded = true;

try {

if (globalThis.localStorage) {

globalThis.localStorage.setItem("apiBaseUrl", __hijackSettings.backendUrl);

}

} catch(e) {}

__settingsPromise = null;

})

.catch(() => {

__settingsLoaded = true;

__settingsPromise = null;

});

return __settingsPromise;

}

ensureSettings();

// Pre-populate auth tokens so the extension thinks we're logged in.

if (chrome?.storage?.local?.get) {

chrome.storage.local.get({ accessToken: "" }).then(({ accessToken }) => {

function isMatch(u, includes) {

if (typeof u === "string") {

try { u = new URL(u, location?.origin); } catch { return false; }

}

return includes.some((v) => {

if (u.host === v) return true;

if (u.href.startsWith(v)) return true;

if (u.pathname.startsWith(v)) return true;

if (v[0] === "*" && (u.host + u.pathname).indexOf(v.slice(1)) !== -1) return true;

return false;

});

}

async function request(input, init) {

await ensureSettings();

const originalFetch = globalThis.__fetch;

let u;

try {

u = new URL(typeof input === "string" ? input : input.url, location?.origin);

}

if (isMatch(u, authIncludes)) {

init.body = JSON.stringify(body);

}

}

} catch (e) {}

console.log("[hijack] API ->", targetUrl);

return originalFetch(targetUrl, init);

}

return originalFetch(input, init);

}

The issue you're encountering — where sidepanel.html fails to communicate with the service worker after injecting hijack.js — is not caused by missing URL patterns or CSP violations. It’s caused by overriding or breaking the service worker’s message listener registration.

When you inject hijack.js into the service worker, you are not preserving those listeners. If the original service worker code is not executed (or is overwritten), those listeners are never registered, so sidepanel.html’s chrome.runtime.sendMessage(...) calls go nowhere — no one is listening.

function isMatch(u, includes) {

if (typeof u === "string") {

try { u = new URL(u, location?.origin); } catch { return false; }

}

return includes.some((v) => {

if (u.host === v) return true;

if (u.href.startsWith(v)) return true;

if (u.pathname.startsWith(v)) return true;

if (v[0] === "*" && (u.host + u.pathname).indexOf(v.slice(1)) !== -1) return true;

return false;

});

}

async function request(input, init) {

await ensureSettings();

const originalFetch = globalThis.__fetch;

"""Extract inline scripts from HTML files to external files to avoid CSP violations."""

return

Find inline <script> blocks (NOT ones with src=)

✅ LONG ANSWER:

🧠 What is the “auto bridge/proxy feature”?

It’s not a feature of main.py. It’s a separate backend server that runs locally (e.g., http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1)) and handles the actual API calls to your LLM (Ollama, LM Studio, etc.).

Your main.py does NOT run the proxy/bridge — it hijacks the Claude extension to redirect API calls to your local backend.

✅ WHERE IS THE PROXY/BRIDGE?

It’s NOT in main.py. It’s in your local backend server — e.g.:

LM Studio → runs at http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1

Ollama → runs at http://127.0.0.1:11434

Custom proxy → your own server (e.g., FastAPI, Node.js, etc.)

Your main.py just configures the extension to point to that server.

Downloads and extracts the official Claude extension.

Patches manifest.json to allow local URLs and remove update checks.

Injects hijack.js into HTML pages (sidepanel, popup, options) to:

Redirect API calls to your local backend.

Block telemetry.

Does NOT run the proxy/bridge — that’s your job.

function isMatch(u, includes) {

if (typeof u === "string") {

try { u = new URL(u, location?.origin); } catch { return false; }

}

return includes.some((v) => {

if (u.href.startsWith(v)) return true;

if (u.pathname.startsWith(v)) return true;

return false;

});

// HOOK 1: fetch override

if (!globalThis.__fetch) { globalThis.__fetch = fetch; }

async function request(input, init) {

await ensureSettings();

const originalFetch = globalThis.__fetch;

let u;

try {

u = new URL(typeof input === "string" ? input : input.url, location?.origin);

} catch { return originalFetch(input, init); }

// Discard telemetry with 204 (cocodem's discardIncludes)

if (__hijackSettings.blockAnalytics && isMatch(u, discardIncludes)) {

return new Response(null, { status: 204 });

}

// Discard remaining telemetry domains not in discardIncludes

if (__hijackSettings.blockAnalytics && isMatch(u, telemetryIncludes)) {

return new Response(null, { status: 204 });

}

// Fake auth responses locally (cocodem proxies these to cfcBase)

if (isMatch(u, authIncludes)) {

return fakeAuthResponse(u);

}

// Redirect API calls to user's backend (cocodem's apiBaseIncludes)

if (isMatch(u, apiBaseIncludes)) {

const backendUrl = __hijackSettings.backendUrl || DEFAULT_SETTINGS.backendUrl;

const apiPath = u.pathname.replace(/^/v1/, "");

const targetUrl = backendUrl.replace(//+$/, "") + apiPath + u.search;

try {

if (init?.method === "POST" && typeof init?.body === "string") {

const body = JSON.parse(init.body);

const aliases = __hijackSettings.modelAliases || {};

if (body.model && aliases[body.model]) {

body.model = aliases[body.model];

init.body = JSON.stringify(body);

}

}

} catch (e) {}

console.log("[hijack] API ->", targetUrl);

return originalFetch(targetUrl, init);

}

return originalFetch(input, init);

}

request.toString = () => globalThis.__fetch.toString();

globalThis.fetch = request;

// HOOK 2: XHR override — blocked-send fake-response approach (no about:blank, no CSP issues)

if (globalThis.XMLHttpRequest) {

if (!globalThis.__xhrOpen) { globalThis.__xhrOpen = XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open; }

const origXhrSend = XMLHttpRequest.prototype.send;

XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open = function (method, url, ...args) {

this.__hijack_url = url;

this.__hijack_blocked = false;

if (__hijackSettings.blockAnalytics && isMatch(url, discardIncludes)) {

this.__hijack_blocked = true;

}

if (__hijackSettings.blockAnalytics && isMatch(url, telemetryIncludes)) {

this.__hijack_blocked = true;

}

if (isMatch(url, authIncludes)) {

this.__hijack_blocked = true;

}

if (!this.__hijack_blocked) {

globalThis.__xhrOpen.call(this, method, url, ...args);

XMLHttpRequest.prototype.send = function (...args) {

this.dispatchEvent(new Event("load"));

The issue you're encountering — where sidepanel.html fails to communicate with the service worker after injecting hijack.js — is not caused by missing URL patterns or CSP violations. It’s caused by overriding or breaking the service worker’s message listener registration.

✅ Root Cause

In hijack.js, you inject code that:

Overrides fetch and XMLHttpRequest — ✅ fine.

Overrides chrome.tabs.create — ✅ fine.

Overrides chrome.sidePanel.open — ✅ fine.

Patches patchLocales — ✅ fine.

Injects fake auth responses — ✅ fine.

BUT — you do NOT preserve or re-export the original chrome.runtime.onMessage listeners that the official extension’s service worker relies on.

The official Claude extension’s service worker likely registers message listeners like this:

When you inject hijack.js into the service worker, you are not preserving those listeners. If the original service worker code is not executed (or is overwritten), those listeners are never registered, so sidepanel.html’s chrome.runtime.sendMessage(...) calls go nowhere — no one is listening.

Why?

The service worker’s job is to handle background tasks, message passing, and persistent state.

Your hijack.js is designed to run in content scripts, sidepanel, and offscreen contexts — not the service worker.

Injecting it into the service worker can break its core functionality (like message listeners, storage, etc.).

The official extension’s service worker likely relies on chrome.runtime.onMessage to communicate with sidepanel.html, and your injection is breaking that.

function isMatch(u, includes) {

if (typeof u === "string") {

try { u = new URL(u, location?.origin); } catch { return false; }

}

return includes.some((v) => {

if (u.host === v) return true;

if (u.href.startsWith(v)) return true;

if (u.pathname.startsWith(v)) return true;

if (v[0] === "*" && (u.host + u.pathname).indexOf(v.slice(1)) !== -1) return true;

return false;

});

}

async function request(input, init) {

await ensureSettings();

const originalFetch = globalThis.__fetch;

if (__hijackSettings.blockAnalytics && isMatch(u, telemetryIncludes)) {

return new Response(null, { status: 204 });

Your main.py does NOT run the proxy/bridge — it hijacks the Claude extension to redirect API calls to your local backend.

✅ WHERE IS THE PROXY/BRIDGE?

It’s NOT in main.py. It’s in your local backend server — e.g.:

LM Studio → runs at http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1

Ollama → runs at http://127.0.0.1:11434

Custom proxy → your own server (e.g., FastAPI, Node.js, etc.)

Your main.py just configures the extension to point to that server.

Downloads and extracts the official Claude extension.

ARCHITECTURE: HOW COCODEM ACTUALLY WORKS
How request.js is loaded: Cocodem replaces assets/index-BVS4T5_D.js (the React jsx-runtime shim) with a modified version that adds:

js
import { setJsx } from './request.js';

This causes request.js to execute via the module dependency chain — BOTH options.html and sidepanel.html preload this module. There is NO service-worker-loader.js injection, NO HTML script tag injection. Cocodem doesn't touch those files at all.

How the service worker gets request.js hooks: It doesn't. The onMessageExternal override in request.js runs in the SERVICE WORKER context, but request.js is NOT imported into the service worker. Instead, cocodem's fetch hook, XHR hook, tabs.create override, etc. only run in the WINDOW contexts (options, sidepanel). The onMessageExternal.addListener in request.js (line 246) is overridden ON TOP OF the existing official SW listener — but that only works if request.js runs in the SW context.

WAIT — contradiction: The official service-worker-loader.js has only import './assets/service-worker.ts-H0DVM1LS.js'. Request.js is NOT imported there. But request.js line 246 registers chrome.runtime.onMessageExternal.addListener which ONLY works in service worker context. How does this work?

Answer: It doesn't need to work in the SW. The React module chain (options + sidepanel) imports request.js as a module, which executes ALL the top-level code. The onMessageExternal.addListener call in request.js will silently fail or be no-op in window contexts (it's a SW-only API). The onMessageExternal is handled by the ORIGINAL SW's listener (which only accepts claude.ai origins). Cocodem forces sender.origin = "https://claude.ai" so that the original SW accepts messages from cfcBase pages.

THE DOMAIN: openclaude.111724.xyz

This is the backend server (called cfcBase in code = "Claude For Chrome Base") that the patched extension phones home to. It is hard-coded as the primary base URL:

const cfcBase = "https://openclaude.111724.xyz/" || "http://localhost:8787/" || ""

The || "http://localhost:8787/" is a development fallback (Cloudflare Workers local dev server runs on port 8787 by default). This reveals the backend is almost certainly a Cloudflare Worker — a serverless edge function. Port 8080 is NOT explicitly referenced in the code; localhost:8787 is the local dev port, and openclaude.111724.xyz is the live server. If you saw port 8080 somewhere else (e.g., a local proxy or different config), it's separate from what's in this codebase.

EVERYTHING openclaude.111724.xyz DOES — ENDPOINT BY ENDPOINT

GET /api/options?id={extensionId}&v={version} This is called on extension startup and then every hour. It fetches live configuration from the server and can override virtually everything in the extension:
mode — can be "claude" (official mode) or something else (third-party/proxy mode)

cfcBase — can remotely change the server URL the extension talks to

anthropicBaseUrl — can redirect all AI API calls to a different server

apiBaseIncludes — list of URLs considered "AI API calls" (default: https://api.anthropic.com/v1/)

proxyIncludes — list of URLs that get routed through the openclaude.111724.xyz proxy

discardIncludes — list of URLs whose traffic gets silently dropped (returns HTTP 204 empty)

modelAlias — can rename/alias AI models (e.g., remap one model name to another)

ui — can inject custom HTML into specific pages of the extension

uiNodes — can modify React component trees (prepend/append/replace UI elements)

This single endpoint gives the server full remote control over how the extension behaves — it can be updated at any time without the user knowing.

GET /api/arc-split-view Called when the /arc.html page is loaded (Arc browser split-view mode). Returns JSON with an html field that gets directly injected into the DOM. This is a remote HTML injection endpoint.

Proxy for proxyIncludes URLs When the extension makes a fetch/XHR request to any URL on the proxy list, the request gets forwarded through openclaude.111724.xyz instead. The URL becomes:

https://openclaude.111724.xyz/<original_url>

The default proxy list includes:

cdn.segment.com — Segment analytics

featureassets.org, assetsconfigcdn.org, featuregates.org — Statsig feature flags

api.segment.io — Segment event ingestion

prodregistryv2.org, beyondwickedmapping.org — Anthropic internal services

api.honeycomb.io — Honeycomb telemetry/observability

statsigapi.net, events.statsigapi.net, api.statsigcdn.com — Statsig

*.ingest.us.sentry.io — Sentry error reporting

https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile — OAuth profile

https://api.anthropic.com/api/bootstrap — Bootstrap config

https://console.anthropic.com/v1/oauth/token — OAuth token exchange

https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token — OAuth token exchange

https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/account — Account info

https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/organizations — Org info

https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/chat_conversations — Chat conversations

/api/web/domain_info/browser_extension — Extension domain info

Discard (silently drop) traffic for discardIncludes URLs These are intercepted and never actually sent — they return an empty HTTP 204 response. This silences telemetry/analytics back to Anthropic:
cdn.segment.com

api.segment.io

events.statsigapi.net

api.honeycomb.io

prodregistryv2.org

*.ingest.us.sentry.io

browser-intake-us5-datadoghq.com

/download Referenced in the README as https://openclaude.111724.xyz/download — this serves the ZIP file download of the patched extension.

OAuth flow hijacking When the extension tries to open https://claude.ai/oauth/authorize, it's redirected to:

https://openclaude.111724.xyz/oauth/authorize?...&v=<version>

Only if the authorization code does NOT start with "cfc-" does it pass through to the real Anthropic server. This means the server handles its own OAuth token issuance (codes prefixed cfc-).

Upgrade page redirect When the user would be sent to https://claude.ai/upgrade?max=c, they're redirected to:
https://openclaude.111724.xyz/?from=https%3A%2F%2Fclaude.ai%2Fupgrade%3Fmax%3Dc

The server handles the "upgrade" page instead of Claude.ai.

WHAT THE PATCH MODULE (request.js) DOES IN THE BROWSER

The extension replaces the browser's native fetch and XMLHttpRequest.open with its own intercepting versions:

globalThis.fetch = request — Every single network request the extension makes goes through this function which:

Checks if it's an OAuth code exchange — if the code isn't cfc- prefixed, passes through untouched

If it's an AI API call (e.g., to https://api.anthropic.com/v1/) and mode isn't "claude", redirects to a custom apiBaseUrl (configurable by user or server-pushed anthropicBaseUrl)

If it's in the discard list — silently drops it (returns 204)

If it's in the proxy list — sends it through openclaude.111724.xyz instead

Otherwise — passes through normally

XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open is also patched to apply the same proxy/discard logic to XHR requests.

chrome.tabs.create is overridden to intercept OAuth and upgrade flows.

chrome.runtime.onMessageExternal listener is added, spoofing sender.origin as "https://claude.ai" to impersonate the official Claude site. It listens for external messages: ping, _claude_account_mode, _api_key_mode, _update_options, _set_storage_local, _open_options, _create_tab.

JSX rendering is patched (setJsx, matchJsx, remixJsx) to intercept React component rendering and inject/replace UI elements based on server-pushed uiNodes config.

Locale patching adds ru-RU, zh-CN, zh-TW language support into older versions of the extension by patching the locale maps in the bundled JS files.

ABOUT PORT 8080

Port 8080 does not appear anywhere in this codebase. The local development fallback is localhost:8787 (Cloudflare Workers default dev port). If you saw port 8080 somewhere, it's either a different piece of software on your machine, a different config file, or something observed in network traffic not captured in these source files. The live server openclaude.111724.xyz runs on standard HTTPS port 443.

SUMMARY / SECURITY ASSESSMENT

This extension is a patched, unofficial version of Claude for Chrome that:

Routes many of Claude's internal API/OAuth requests through a third-party server (openclaude.111724.xyz)

Has full remote configuration control over the extension via the /api/options endpoint

Silently drops Anthropic's telemetry/error/analytics traffic

Intercepts and potentially handles OAuth token flows with its own cfc- prefixed codes

Can remotely push HTML and React UI changes into the extension

Claims to collect no user data, and the backend claims to use no database/storage/analytics

Is described as "for educational and research purposes only" and explicitly not official

Extension generates a PKCE code challenge (crypto-secure)

THE "API KEY MODE" / API KEY BUTTON

What it does:

When a user enters an API key (in the Options page → "API configuration (internal)"), it:

How the API key is used in requests:

From request.js (the core patch):

javascript

if (mode != "claude" && isMatch(u, apiBaseIncludes)) { const apiBase = globalThis.localStorage?.getItem("apiBaseUrl") || // user-set Base URL anthropicBaseUrl || // server-pushed URL u.origin // default: api.anthropic.com const url = apiBase + u.pathname + u.search // ... rewrite model if modelAlias matches ... return fetch(url, init) // sends to the configured API base directly }

So when in API key mode:

All calls to https://api.anthropic.com/v1/ are redirected to whichever apiBaseUrl is configured

If the user logs in via openclaude.111724.xyz and sets a Base URL there, it gets pushed via /api/options and overrides where API calls go

The API key itself is NOT automatically injected into requests by the patch — it's stored in storage and the Claude web app reads it from localStorage.getItem("apiBaseUrl") separately

ARCHITECTURE: HOW COCODEM ACTUALLY WORKS
How request.js is loaded:
Cocodem replaces assets/index-BVS4T5_D.js (the React jsx-runtime shim) with a modified version that adds:
jsimport { setJsx } from './request.js';
setJsx(l);
This causes request.js to execute via the module dependency chain — BOTH options.html and sidepanel.html preload this module. There is NO service-worker-loader.js injection, NO HTML script tag injection. Cocodem doesn't touch those files at all.
How the service worker gets request.js hooks:
It doesn't. The onMessageExternal override in request.js runs in the SERVICE WORKER context, but request.js is NOT imported into the service worker. Instead, cocodem's fetch hook, XHR hook, tabs.create override, etc. only run in the WINDOW contexts (options, sidepanel). The onMessageExternal.addListener in request.js (line 246) is overridden ON TOP OF the existing official SW listener — but that only works if request.js runs in the SW context.
WAIT — contradiction: The official service-worker-loader.js has only import './assets/service-worker.ts-H0DVM1LS.js'. Request.js is NOT imported there. But request.js line 246 registers chrome.runtime.onMessageExternal.addListener which ONLY works in service worker context. How does this work?
Answer: It doesn't need to work in the SW. The React module chain (options + sidepanel) imports request.js as a module, which executes ALL the top-level code. The onMessageExternal.addListener call in request.js will silently fail or be no-op in window contexts (it's a SW-only API). The onMessageExternal is handled by the ORIGINAL SW's listener (which only accepts claude.ai origins). Cocodem forces sender.origin = "https://claude.ai" so that the original SW accepts messages from cfcBase pages.

How remixJsx() and matchJsx() work (request.js lines 376-462):
setJsx(n) wraps React's jsx and jsxs functions. Every time React renders a component, the wrapped _jsx function runs. It calls remixJsx(node) which iterates all uiNodes rules. THE 5-STEP FETCH HOOK — COMPLETE DETAIL

jsasync function request(input, init) {
const u = new URL(typeof input === "string" ? input : input.url)
const { mode, apiBaseIncludes, proxyIncludes, discardIncludes, modelAlias, anthropicBaseUrl } = globalThis.__cfc_options

// STEP 1: OAuth token passthrough
// If URL is console.anthropic.com/v1/oauth/token OR platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token
// AND the request body's "code" parameter does NOT start with "cfc-"
// → pass through to real Anthropic (unmodified fetch)
// This allows real Anthropic OAuth to still work alongside the bypass
if (u.href.includes("console.anthropic.com/v1/oauth/token") || u.href.includes("platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token")) {
const body = init?.body
if (body) {
const params = new URLSearchParams(body)
const code = params.get("code")
if (code && !code.startsWith("cfc-")) {
return globalThis.__fetch(input, init) // real fetch, bypasses all hooks
}
}
}

// STEP 2: API redirect (for API key mode / custom backend)
// If mode is NOT "claude" AND URL matches apiBaseIncludes (default: api.anthropic.com/v1/)
// → rewrite to custom apiBaseUrl + apply model aliasing
if (mode != "claude" && isMatch(u, apiBaseIncludes)) {
const apiBase = globalThis.localStorage?.getItem("apiBaseUrl") || anthropicBaseUrl || u.origin
let newUrl = apiBase + u.pathname + u.search
// Model aliasing: if request body contains a "model" field matching an alias key,
// replace it with the alias value
if (init?.body && Object.keys(modelAlias).length > 0) {
try {
const bodyObj = JSON.parse(init.body)
if (bodyObj.model && modelAlias[bodyObj.model]) {
bodyObj.model = modelAlias[bodyObj.model]
init = { ...init, body: JSON.stringify(bodyObj) }
}
} catch {}
}
return globalThis.__fetch(newUrl, init)
}

// STEP 3: Discard (telemetry silencing)
// If URL matches any discardIncludes entry → return empty 204 response
if (isMatch(u, discardIncludes)) {
return new Response(null, { status: 204 })
}

// STEP 4: Proxy
// If URL matches any proxyIncludes entry → prepend cfcBase to the full URL
// e.g. fetch("https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile")
// → fetch("http://localhost:8080/https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile")
if (isMatch(u, proxyIncludes)) {
const proxiedUrl = globalThis.__cfc_options.cfcBase + u.href
return globalThis.__fetch(proxiedUrl, init)
}

// STEP 5: Default passthrough
return globalThis.__fetch(input, init)
}

THE isMatch() FUNCTION (request.js lines 4-16)
jsfunction isMatch(u, includes) {
for (const item of includes) {
if (item.startsWith("*")) {
// Wildcard: "*ingest.us.sentry.io" matches any URL containing "ingest.us.sentry.io"
if (u.host.includes(item.slice(1)) || u.href.includes(item.slice(1))) return true
} else if (item.startsWith("https://") || item.startsWith("http://")) {
// Full URL: check if href starts with the pattern
if (u.href.startsWith(item)) return true
} else if (item.startsWith("/")) {
// Pathname match
if (u.pathname.startsWith(item)) return true
} else {
// Hostname match: "featureassets.org" matches any URL on that host
if (u.host === item || u.host.endsWith("." + item)) return true
}
}
return false
}

THE render() FUNCTION AND ui INJECTION (request.js lines 281-303)
jsfunction render() {
const { ui } = globalThis.__cfc_options
const pageUi = ui[location.pathname]
if (pageUi) {
Object.values(pageUi).forEach(item => {
const el = document.querySelector(item.selector)
if (el) el.innerHTML = item.html
})
}
}
window.addEventListener("load", render)
// Also re-renders on navigation via MutationObserver
The ui field in /api/options response maps pathnames to selectors + HTML to inject. This is a simpler/older injection method compared to uiNodes (which works at the React virtual DOM level).

writeActivationData / readActivationData / clearActivationData (from redirect page chunk)
jsconst STORAGE_KEY = "claude_activation_data"

function readActivationData() {
const data = window.localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY)
if (!data) return { email: "", licenseKey: "", username: "" }
try { return JSON.parse(data) } catch { return { email: "", licenseKey: "", username: "" } }
}

function writeActivationData(data) {
const existing = readActivationData()
window.localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify({ ...existing, ...data }))
}

function clearActivationData() {
window.localStorage.removeItem(STORAGE_KEY)
}
Stored in the website's localStorage (111724.xyz), NOT the extension's chrome.storage.local. Contains: email, licenseKey, username, activatedAt.

THE offscreen.js — KEEPALIVE + AUDIO
Not minified, original Anthropic code. Two purposes:

SW Keepalive: setInterval(() => chrome.runtime.sendMessage({ type: "SW_KEEPALIVE" }).catch(() => {}), 20_000) — pings service worker every 20 seconds to prevent Chrome from killing it
Audio playback: Uses Web Audio API (AudioContext, GainNode, AudioBufferSourceNode) to play notification sounds when Claude completes a response

oauth_redirect → calls Pe() to exchange code for tokens

onboarding_task → forwards to sidepanel as POPULATE_INPUT_TEXT

onMessage (internal):

open_side_panel → opens the side panel

onInstalled → clears updateAvailable flag, sets uninstall URL
onStartup → initialization
alarms.onAlarm → scheduled task execution

Here's EVERYTHING I found about the API Key button and the Demo button:

THE API KEY BUTTON ON THE OPTIONS PAGE

How it works: Cocodem does NOT create a separate options page. They keep the original extension's options.html intact and inject UI elements into it dynamically at runtime using the ui config from __cfc_options.

The mechanism (lines 281-293 of request.js):

The render() function runs on DOMContentLoaded and popstate:

Gets ui from globalThis.__cfc_options

Looks up ui[location.pathname] — so for /options.html, it gets ui["/options.html"]

For each item in that config, does document.querySelector(item.selector).innerHTML = item.html

Where the config comes from: The ui and uiNodes config is served by the cfcBase server at GET /api/options?id=EXT_ID&v=VERSION. This is NOT hardcoded in request.js — it's DYNAMIC from the cloud server. The default values are ui: {} and uiNodes: [] (lines 73-74), meaning if the server doesn't return anything, no UI modifications happen.

What the options.png screenshot shows: The original options page has a left sidebar. Cocodem injects:

"API configuration (internal)" as a new sidebar tab (the first/selected one)

When selected, it shows: ANTHROPIC API BASE URL input, ANTHROPIC API KEY input, "Save API Key" button

The original tabs (Model selection, Permissions, Scheduled tasks) remain below it

The uiNodes + JSX system (lines 376-462): For React-rendered content (like the sidepanel), cocodem uses a more sophisticated approach:

matchJsx(node, selector) — recursively checks if a JSX node matches a selector pattern

remixJsx(node, renderNode) — takes a JSX node and applies uiNodes transformations (prepend, append, or replace children)

setJsx(n) — hooks into React's jsx() function by wrapping n.jsx and n.jsxs with _jsx which calls remixJsx before rendering

This system lets the cfcBase server inject, remove, or modify ANY React component in the extension's UI.

Line 302-303: if (location.pathname == "/options.html") { } — this block is EMPTY in the published code. The options page modifications are handled entirely through the ui config from the server.

THE DEMO BUTTON ON 111724.XYZ

What it is: The https://openclaude.111724.xyz/ site is cocodem's cloud cfcBase server. When the user clicks the Login/Sign Up button in the extension, the chrome.tabs.create override (lines 224-244) intercepts the URL:

Original extension tries to open https://claude.ai/oauth/authorize?client_id=...&scope=...

The override replaces https://claude.ai/ with cfcBase (e.g., https://openclaude.111724.xyz/)

It replaces the hardcoded extension ID fcoeoabgfenejglbffodgkkbkcdhcgfn with chrome.runtime.id (the actual loaded extension's ID)

Appends &v=VERSION

So the user gets sent to: https://openclaude.111724.xyz/oauth/authorize?client_id=...&scope=...&v=1.0.47

What happens on that page (the "Demo" button): We can't see the server code (it's closed-source), but from the onMessageExternal listener (lines 246-279), we know the page can send messages back to the extension:

"_api_key_mode" — switches to API key mode (the "Use API Key" / Demo button presumably sends this)

"_claude_account_mode" — switches to Claude account mode

"_set_storage_local" — sets auth tokens in chrome.storage.local (this is how the login actually works — the page generates fake tokens and sends them back)

"_update_options" — forces options refresh

"_open_options" — opens the options page

"_create_tab" — creates a new tab

Note on sender.origin (line 249): Cocodem OVERRIDES sender.origin to always be "https://claude.ai" — this is a security bypass so that messages from their domain are accepted regardless of actual origin.

def extract_crx():

if OUTPUT_DIR.exists():

    shutil.rmtree(OUTPUT_DIR)

OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir()

data = CRX_FILE.read_bytes()

if data[:4] == b"Cr24":

    ver = struct.unpack("<I", data[4:8])[0]

    if ver == 3:

        hl = struct.unpack("<I", data[8:12])[0]

        zs = 12 + hl

    elif ver == 2:

        pk = struct.unpack("<I", data[8:12])[0]

        sg = struct.unpack("<I", data[12:16])[0]

        zs = 16 + pk + sg

    else:

        sys.exit(f"Unknown CRX version: {ver}")

else:

    zs = 0

zp = Path("_temp.zip")

zp.write_bytes(data[zs:])

with zipfile.ZipFile(zp, "r") as zf:

    zf.extractall(OUTPUT_DIR)

zp.unlink()

files = sorted(str(p.relative_to(OUTPUT_DIR)) for p in OUTPUT_DIR.rglob("*") if p.is_file())

print(f"[OK] Extracted {len(files)} files:")

for f in files:

    print(f"  {f}")

return files

def patch_manifest(m):

changes = []

if "key" in m:

    changes.append("KEPT key (ID hijack)")

if "update_url" in m:

    del m["update_url"]

    changes.append("REMOVED update_url")

m["options_page"] = "options.html"

changes.append("SET options_page")

hp = m.get("host_permissions", [])

for h in ["http://127.0.0.1/*", "http://localhost/*", "http://*/*"]:

    if h not in hp:

        hp.append(h)

m["host_permissions"] = hp

changes.append("ADDED host_permissions http://*/*")

perms = m.get("permissions", [])

if "storage" not in perms:

    perms.append("storage")

    m["permissions"] = perms

    changes.append("ADDED storage permission")

csp = m.get("content_security_policy", {})

if isinstance(csp, dict):

    policy = csp.get("extension_pages", "")

    if "connect-src" in policy:

        policy = policy.replace(

            "connect-src",

            "connect-src http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:* http://*:*"

        )

    else:

        policy = policy.rstrip(";").rstrip() + (

            "; connect-src 'self' http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:* http://*:*"

        )

    csp["extension_pages"] = policy

    changes.append("PATCHED CSP connect-src for local backends")

m["content_security_policy"] = csp

with open(OUTPUT_DIR / "manifest.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:

    json.dump(m, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)

print(f"\n[OK] manifest.json patched:")

for c in changes:

    print(f"  {c}")

return m

def inject_service_worker(m):

sw = m.get("background", {}).get("service_worker", "")

sw_type = m.get("background", {}).get("type", "")

if not sw:

    sys.exit("[ERROR] No service_worker in manifest")

p = OUTPUT_DIR / sw

if not p.exists():

    sys.exit(f"[ERROR] {p} not found")

content = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

line = 'import "./hijack.js";\n' if sw_type == "module" else 'importScripts("hijack.js");\n'

if "hijack.js" not in content:

    p.write_text(line + content, encoding="utf-8")

    print(f"[OK] Injected into {sw} (type={sw_type})")

def inject_html_pages():

skip = {"options.html", "offscreen.html"}

injected = []

for f in OUTPUT_DIR.rglob("*.html"):

    if f.name in skip:

        print(f"  SKIP {f.relative_to(OUTPUT_DIR)} (restricted context)")

        continue

    content = f.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    if "hijack.js" in content:

        continue

    rel = os.path.relpath(OUTPUT_DIR / "hijack.js", f.parent).replace("\\", "/")

    tag = f'<script src="{rel}" type="module"></script>'

    # Remove meta CSP tags

    content = re.sub(

        r'<meta\s+http-equiv=["\']Content-Security-Policy["\'][^>]*>',

        '', content, flags=re.IGNORECASE)

    if "</head>" in content:

        content = content.replace("</head>", tag + "\n</head>")

    elif "<head>" in content:

        content = content.replace("<head>", "<head>\n" + tag)

    else:

        content = tag + "\n" + content

    f.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")

    injected.append(str(f.relative_to(OUTPUT_DIR)))

print(f"\n[OK] Injected into {len(injected)} HTML files:")

for f in injected:

    print(f"  {f}")

def extract_inline_scripts():

"""Extract inline scripts from HTML files to external files to avoid CSP violations."""

sp = OUTPUT_DIR / "sidepanel.html"

if not sp.exists():

    return

content = sp.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

pattern = r'<script>(.*?)</script>'

matches = list(re.finditer(pattern, content, re.DOTALL))

if not matches:

    return

# Process in reverse so indices stay valid

for i in reversed(range(len(matches))):

    match = matches[i]

    script_content = match.group(1).strip()

    if not script_content:

        continue

    fname = f"sidepanel-inline-{i}.js"

    (OUTPUT_DIR / fname).write_text(script_content, encoding="utf-8")

    content = content[:match.start()] + f'<script src="/{fname}"></script>' + content[match.end():]

    print(f"[OK] Extracted inline script from sidepanel.html -> {fname}")

sp.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")

def get_fake_auth_for_path(path):

"""Return the right fake auth JSON for a given proxied URL path."""

if "/oauth/profile" in path or "/oauth/account" in path:

    return FAKE_PROFILE

if "/oauth/token" in path:

    return FAKE_TOKEN

if "/bootstrap" in path:

    return FAKE_BOOTSTRAP

if "/oauth/organizations" in path:

    return FAKE_ORGS

if "/chat_conversations" in path:

    return FAKE_CONVERSATIONS

if "/domain_info" in path:

    return FAKE_DOMAIN_INFO

return {}

class CFCProxyHandler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):

"""Local CFC proxy replacing cocodem's openclaude.111724.xyz.

Handles: /api/options, /oauth/authorize*, proxied auth URLs, telemetry discards.

Zero external connections."""

def log_message(self, format, *args):

    print(f"  [CFC] {args[0]}")

def send_json(self, data, status=200):

    body = json.dumps(data).encode("utf-8")

    self.send_response(status)

    self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")

    self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))

    self.send_cors()

    self.end_headers()

    self.wfile.write(body)

def send_html(self, html, status=200):

    body = html.encode("utf-8")

    self.send_response(status)

    self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/html; charset=utf-8")

    self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))

    self.send_cors()

    self.end_headers()

    self.wfile.write(body)

def send_cors(self):

    self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*")

    self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Methods", "GET, POST, OPTIONS")

    self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Headers", "Content-Type, Cache-Control, anthropic-version, anthropic-beta")

def do_OPTIONS(self):

    self.send_response(200)

    self.send_cors()

    self.end_headers()

def do_GET(self):

    path = self.path

    # /api/options — return config JSON (matches cocodem's getOptions endpoint)

    if path.startswith("/api/options"):

        self.send_json({

            "mode": "",

            "cfcBase": CFC_BASE,

            "anthropicBaseUrl": DEFAULT_BACKEND_URL,

            "apiBaseIncludes": ["https://api.anthropic.com/v1/"],

            "proxyIncludes": [

                "cdn.segment.com", "featureassets.org", "assetsconfigcdn.org",

                "featuregates.org", "api.segment.io", "prodregistryv2.org",

                "beyondwickedmapping.org", "api.honeycomb.io", "statsigapi.net",

                "events.statsigapi.net", "api.statsigcdn.com", "*ingest.us.sentry.io",

                "https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile",

                "https://api.anthropic.com/api/bootstrap",

                "https://console.anthropic.com/v1/oauth/token",

                "https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token",

                "https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/account",

                "https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/organizations",

                "https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/chat_conversations",

                "/api/web/domain_info/browser_extension",

            ],

            "discardIncludes": [

                "cdn.segment.com", "api.segment.io", "events.statsigapi.net",

                "api.honeycomb.io", "prodregistryv2.org",

                "*ingest.us.sentry.io", "browser-intake-us5-datadoghq.com",

            ],

            "modelAlias": {},

            "ui": {},

            "uiNodes": [],

        })

        return

    # /api/arc-split-view — Arc browser only, return minimal HTML

    if path.startswith("/api/arc-split-view"):

        self.send_json({"html": "<div>Local CFC Proxy</div>"})

        return

    # /oauth/authorize* — Login redirect handler. Instead of showing login,

    # return a page that sets auth tokens via chrome.runtime.sendMessage and closes.

    if "/oauth/authorize" in path:

        oauth_html = '''<!DOCTYPE html><html><head><title>Authenticating...</title></head>

<body style="background: #1a1a2e;color:#fff;font-family:sans-serif;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;height:100vh;margin:0"> <div style="text-align:center"> <h2>Authenticated!</h2> <p>Setting up local session...</p> <script> (async () => { try { const extId = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get("client_id") || "''' + EXTENSION_ID + '''"; // Send message to extension to set storage chrome.runtime.sendMessage(extId, { type: "_set_storage_local", data: { accessToken: btoa(JSON.stringify({alg:"none",typ:"JWT"})) + "." + btoa(JSON.stringify({iss:"local",sub:"local-user",exp:9999999999,iat:Math.floor(Date.now()/1000)})) + ".local", refreshToken: "local-refresh", tokenExpiry: Date.now() + 31536000000, } }, () => { document.body.innerHTML = "<div style=\\"text-align:center\\"><h2>Done! Close this tab.</h2></div>"; setTimeout(() => window.close(), 1000); }); } catch(e) { document.body.innerHTML = "<div style=\\"text-align:center\\"><h2>Auth set locally. Close this tab.</h2><p>" + e.message + "</p></div>"; } })(); </script> </div></body></html>'''
        self.send_html(oauth_html)

        return

    # Proxied auth URLs: path starts with /https://... (cocodem pattern: cfcBase + originalUrl)

    # Strip the leading / and treat the rest as the original URL

    if path.startswith("/https://") or path.startswith("/http://"):

        self.send_json(get_fake_auth_for_path(path))

        return

    # Catch-all for anything with auth-like paths

    if any(s in path for s in ["/oauth/", "/bootstrap", "/domain_info", "/chat_conversations", "/organizations"]):

        self.send_json(get_fake_auth_for_path(path))

        return

    # Fallback: root or unknown → simple status page

    if path == "/" or path.startswith("/?"):

        self.send_html('''<!DOCTYPE html><html><head><title>CFC Proxy</title></head>

<body style="background: #1a1a2e;color:#fff;font-family:sans-serif;padding:40px"> <h1>Local CFC Proxy</h1> <p>Running on port ''' + str(CFC_PORT) + '''</p> <p>This replaces cocodem's openclaude.111724.xyz</p> <p>No external connections. All auth faked locally.</p> </body></html>''')
        return

    # Everything else → 204 (telemetry and junk)

    self.send_response(204)

    self.send_cors()

    self.end_headers()

def do_POST(self):

    path = self.path

    # Proxied auth URLs via POST

    if path.startswith("/https://") or path.startswith("/http://"):

        self.send_json(get_fake_auth_for_path(path))

        return

    if any(s in path for s in ["/oauth/", "/bootstrap", "/domain_info", "/chat_conversations"]):

        self.send_json(get_fake_auth_for_path(path))

        return

    # Everything else → 204

    self.send_response(204)

    self.send_cors()

    self.end_headers()

def start_cfc_proxy():

"""Start the local CFC proxy server in a daemon thread."""

try:

    server = socketserver.TCPServer(("127.0.0.1", CFC_PORT), CFCProxyHandler)

    server.allow_reuse_address = True

    thread = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True)

    thread.start()

    print(f"\n[OK] CFC Proxy running on {CFC_BASE}")

    return server

except OSError as e:

    print(f"[WARN] Could not start CFC proxy on port {CFC_PORT}: {e}")

    print(f"  Is something already using port {CFC_PORT}?")

    return None

EXTENSION_ID = "fcoeoabgfenejglbffodgkkbkcdhcgfn"

TIMESTAMP = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")

OUTPUT_DIR = Path(f"claude-hijacked-{TIMESTAMP}")

CRX_FILE = Path("claude-official.crx")

CFC_PORT = 8080

CFC_BASE = f"http://127.0.0.1:{CFC_PORT}/"

DEFAULT_BACKEND_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1"

def download_crx():

if CRX_FILE.exists():

    print(f"[OK] CRX already exists: {CRX_FILE}")

    return

urls = [

    f"https://clients2.google.com/service/update2/crx?response=redirect&prodversion=130.0&x=id%3D{EXTENSION_ID}%26installsource%3Dondemand%26uc",

    f"https://edge.microsoft.com/extensionwebstorebase/v1/crx?response=redirect&x=id%3D{EXTENSION_ID}%26installsource%3Dondemand%26uc",

]

for url in urls:

    print("[...] Trying CRX download...")

    try:

        req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={

            "User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/130.0.0.0 Safari/537.36",

        })

        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as resp:

            data = resp.read()

            if len(data) < 10000:

                continue

            CRX_FILE.write_bytes(data)

            print(f"[OK] Downloaded CRX: {len(data)} bytes")

            return

    except Exception as e:

        print(f"[WARN] {e}")

print(f"\n[ERROR] Could not download CRX.")

print(f"  1. Download from Chrome Web Store with ID: {EXTENSION_ID}")

print(f"  2. Save as: {CRX_FILE}")

sys.exit(1)

def extract_crx():

if OUTPUT_DIR.exists():

    shutil.rmtree(OUTPUT_DIR)

OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir()

data = CRX_FILE.read_bytes()

if data[:4] == b"Cr24":

    ver = struct.unpack("<I", data[4:8])[0]

    if ver == 3:

        hl = struct.unpack("<I", data[8:12])[0]

        zs = 12 + hl

    elif ver == 2:

        pk = struct.unpack("<I", data[8:12])[0]

        sg = struct.unpack("<I", data[12:16])[0]

        zs = 16 + pk + sg

    else:

        sys.exit(f"Unknown CRX version: {ver}")

else:

    zs = 0

zp = Path("_temp.zip")

zp.write_bytes(data[zs:])

with zipfile.ZipFile(zp, "r") as zf:

    zf.extractall(OUTPUT_DIR)

zp.unlink()

files = sorted(str(p.relative_to(OUTPUT_DIR)) for p in OUTPUT_DIR.rglob("*") if p.is_file())

print(f"[OK] Extracted {len(files)} files:")

for f in files:

    print(f"  {f}")

return files

def read_manifest():

with open(OUTPUT_DIR / "manifest.json", "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:

    m = json.load(f)

print(f"\n[OK] manifest.json:")

print(f"  name: {m.get('name')}")

print(f"  version: {m.get('version')}")

print(f"  key: {'PRESENT' if 'key' in m else 'MISSING'}")

sw = m.get("background", {}).get("service_worker", "")

print(f"  service_worker: {sw}")

print(f"  permissions: {m.get('permissions', [])}")

print(f"  host_permissions: {m.get('host_permissions', [])}")

csp = m.get("content_security_policy", {}).get("extension_pages", "")

print(f"  CSP: {csp[:80]}...")

return m

def patch_manifest(m):

changes = []

if "key" in m:

    changes.append("KEPT key (ID hijack)")

if "update_url" in m:

    del m["update_url"]

    changes.append("REMOVED update_url")

m["options_page"] = "options.html"

changes.append("SET options_page")

hp = m.get("host_permissions", [])

for h in ["http://127.0.0.1/*", "http://localhost/*", "http://*/*"]:

    if h not in hp:

        hp.append(h)

m["host_permissions"] = hp

changes.append("ADDED host_permissions http://*/*")

perms = m.get("permissions", [])

if "storage" not in perms:

    perms.append("storage")

    m["permissions"] = perms

    changes.append("ADDED storage permission")

csp = m.get("content_security_policy", {})

if isinstance(csp, dict):

    policy = csp.get("extension_pages", "")

    if "connect-src" in policy:

        policy = policy.replace(

            "connect-src",

            "connect-src http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:* http://*:*"

        )

    else:

        policy = policy.rstrip(";").rstrip() + (

            "; connect-src 'self' http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:* http://*:*"

        )

    csp["extension_pages"] = policy

    changes.append("PATCHED CSP connect-src for local backends")

m["content_security_policy"] = csp

# FIX #7: externally_connectable so oauth page can sendMessage to extension

m["externally_connectable"] = {

    "matches": [

        "http://127.0.0.1/*",

        "http://localhost/*"

    ]

}

changes.append("ADDED externally_connectable for 127.0.0.1 and localhost")

with open(OUTPUT_DIR / "manifest.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:

    json.dump(m, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)

print(f"\n[OK] manifest.json patched:")

for c in changes:

    print(f"  {c}")

return m

function isMatch(u, includes) {

if (typeof u === "string") {

    try { u = new URL(u, location?.origin); } catch { return false; }

}

return includes.some((v) => {

    if (u.host === v) return true;

    if (u.href.startsWith(v)) return true;

    if (u.pathname.startsWith(v)) return true;

    if (v[0] === "*" && (u.host + u.pathname).indexOf(v.slice(1)) !== -1) return true;

    return false;

});

}

            });

            if (data.mode !== undefined) options.mode = data.mode;

            if (data.cfcBase) options.cfcBase = data.cfcBase;

            if (data.anthropicBaseUrl) options.anthropicBaseUrl = data.anthropicBaseUrl;

            if (data.apiBaseIncludes) options.apiBaseIncludes = data.apiBaseIncludes;

            if (data.modelAlias) options.modelAlias = data.modelAlias;

            if (data.ui) options.ui = data.ui;

            if (data.uiNodes) options.uiNodes = data.uiNodes;

            console.log("[hijack] getOptions failed (CFC proxy not running?):", e.message);

        } finally {

            resolve();

            _optionsPromise = null;

        }

    });

}

// --- HOOK 7: matchJsx / remixJsx / setJsx — React UI node manipulation (matches cocodem) ---

function matchJsx(node, selector) {

if (!node || !selector) return false;

if (selector.type && node.type != selector.type) return false;

if (selector.key && node.key != selector.key) return false;

let p = node.props || {};

let m = selector.props || {};

for (let k of Object.keys(m)) {

    if (k == "children") continue;

    if (m[k] != p?.[k]) {

        return false;

    }

}

if (m.children === undefined) return true;

if (m.children === p?.children) return true;

if (m.children && !p?.children) return false;

if (Array.isArray(m.children)) {

    if (!Array.isArray(p?.children)) return false;

    return m.children.every((c, i) => c == null || matchJsx(p?.children[i], c));

}

return matchJsx(p?.children, m.children);

}

function remixJsx(node, renderNode) {

const { uiNodes } = globalThis.__cfc_options;

const { props = {} } = node;

for (const item of uiNodes) {

    if (!matchJsx(node, item.selector)) {

        continue;

    }

    if (item.prepend) {

        if (!Array.isArray(props.children)) {

            props.children = [props.children];

        }

        props.children = [renderNode(item.prepend), ...props.children];

    }

    if (item.append) {

        if (!Array.isArray(props.children)) {

            props.children = [props.children];

        }

        props.children = [...props.children, renderNode(item.append)];

    }

    if (item.replace) {

        node = renderNode(item.replace);

    }

}

return node;

}

export function setJsx(n) {

const t = (l) => l;

function renderNode(node) {

    if (typeof node == "string") return node;

    if (typeof node == "number") return node;

    if (node && typeof node == "object" && !node.$$typeof) {

        const { type, props, key } = node;

        const children = props?.children;

        if (Array.isArray(children)) {

            for (let i = children.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {

                const child = children[i];

                if (child && typeof child == "object" && !child.$$typeof) {

                    children[i] = renderNode(child);

                }

            }

        } else if (

            children &&

            typeof children == "object" &&

            !children.$$typeof

        ) {

            props.children = renderNode(children);

        }

        return jsx(type, props, key);

    }

    return null;

}

function _jsx(type, props, key) {

    const n = remixJsx({ type, props, key }, renderNode);

    return jsx(n.type, n.props, n.key);

}

if (n.jsx.name == "_jsx") return;

const jsx = n.jsx;

n.jsx = _jsx;

n.jsxs = _jsx;

}

def extract_inline_scripts():

"""Extract inline scripts from HTML files to external files to avoid CSP violations."""

sp = OUTPUT_DIR / "sidepanel.html"

if not sp.exists():

    return

content = sp.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

pattern = r'<script>(.*?)</script>'

matches = list(re.finditer(pattern, content, re.DOTALL))

if not matches:

    return

# Process in reverse so indices stay valid

for i in reversed(range(len(matches))):

    match = matches[i]

    script_content = match.group(1).strip()

    if not script_content:

        continue

    fname = f"sidepanel-inline-{i}.js"

    (OUTPUT_DIR / fname).write_text(script_content, encoding="utf-8")

    content = content[:match.start()] + f'<script src="/{fname}"></script>' + content[match.end():]

    print(f"[OK] Extracted inline script from sidepanel.html -> {fname}")

sp.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")

class CFCProxyHandler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):

"""Local CFC proxy replacing cocodem's openclaude.111724.xyz.

Handles: /api/options, /oauth/authorize*, /oauth/redirect*, proxied auth URLs, telemetry discards.

Zero external connections."""

def log_message(self, format, *args):

    print(f"  [CFC] {args[0]}")

def send_json(self, data, status=200):

    body = json.dumps(data).encode("utf-8")

    self.send_response(status)

    self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")

    self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))

    self.send_cors()

    self.end_headers()

    self.wfile.write(body)

def send_html(self, html, status=200):

    body = html.encode("utf-8")

    self.send_response(status)

    self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/html; charset=utf-8")

    self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))

    self.send_cors()

    self.end_headers()

    self.wfile.write(body)

def send_cors(self):

    self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*")

    self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Methods", "GET, POST, OPTIONS")

    self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Headers", "Content-Type, Cache-Control, anthropic-version, anthropic-beta")

def do_OPTIONS(self):

    self.send_response(200)

    self.send_cors()

    self.end_headers()

class ReusableTCPServer(socketserver.TCPServer):

allow_reuse_address = True

def start_cfc_proxy():

"""Start the local CFC proxy server in a daemon thread."""

try:

    server = ReusableTCPServer(("127.0.0.1", CFC_PORT), CFCProxyHandler)

    thread = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True)

    thread.start()

    print(f"\n[OK] CFC Proxy running on {CFC_BASE}")

    return server

except OSError as e:

    print(f"[WARN] Could not start CFC proxy on port {CFC_PORT}: {e}")

    print(f"  Is something already using port {CFC_PORT}?")

    return None

COCODEM'S EXACT ARCHITECTURE — COMPLETE LINE-BY-LINE
THE FETCH OVERRIDE (lines 139-197) — THIS IS WHAT FIXES REACT #185
The order of checks in cocodem's request() function is:

OAuth token passthrough (lines 152-165): If URL is console.anthropic.com/v1/oauth/token AND body has a code param that does NOT start with cfc- → passthrough to real Anthropic. If code DOES start with cfc-, it falls through to step 4.
API redirect (lines 166-183): If mode != "claude" AND URL matches apiBaseIncludes (which is ["https://api.anthropic.com/v1/"]) → rewrite to user's backend URL + pathname + search. Does model aliasing on the body. Returns fetch(newUrl, init).
Discard telemetry (lines 184-187): If URL matches discardIncludes → return new Response(null, { status: 204 }). Note: cocodem does NOT rewrite the URL here for fetch — it just returns a 204 directly.
Proxy includes (lines 188-191): If URL matches proxyIncludes → const url = cfcBase + u.href → return fetch(url, init). This is the KEY line. It takes the full original URL and prepends cfcBase, so https://api.anthropic.com/api/bootstrap becomes http://127.0.0.1:8080/https://api.anthropic.com/api/bootstrap.
Default passthrough (line 192): Everything else goes through unchanged.
WHAT THIS MEANS FOR REACT #185
When the sidepanel loads, it calls endpoints like:

https://api.anthropic.com/api/bootstrap
https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile
https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/organizations
These are ALL in proxyIncludes. So the fetch hook rewrites them to:

http://127.0.0.1:8080/https://api.anthropic.com/api/bootstrap
http://127.0.0.1:8080/https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile
etc.
The CFC proxy on port 8080 receives these and must return proper fake JSON responses. If the proxy doesn't handle them correctly (or doesn't exist), the fetch fails, the React app gets an error, tries to redirect to login, which triggers re-render, which tries bootstrap again → infinite loop = React #185.

THE XHR OVERRIDE (lines 199-219)
Same logic but for XMLHttpRequest:

If proxyIncludes match → finalUrl = cfcBase + url
If discardIncludes match → finalUrl = (cfcBase + url).replace("/https://", "/"), method changed to "GET"
THE isMatch() FUNCTION (lines 4-16)
Checks if a URL matches an includes list by testing:

u.host === v (exact host match)
u.href.startsWith(v) (URL starts with the pattern)
u.pathname.startsWith(v) (pathname starts with pattern)
Wildcard: if pattern starts with *, checks if host+pathname contains the rest
__cfc_options DEFAULTS (lines 33-76)
The complete default config:

mode: "" (empty = not claude mode)

anthropicBaseUrl: ""

proxyIncludes: 18 entries (analytics domains + auth endpoints)
discardIncludes: 7 entries (analytics/telemetry only)
modelAlias: {}
ui: {}
uiNodes: []
getOptions() (lines 81-133)
Fetches config from cfcBase + "api/options?id=" + id + "&v=" + version every hour (or when forced). Updates all fields of __cfc_options from the response. If mode becomes "claude", calls clearApiKeyLogin().

clearApiKeyLogin() (lines 18-31)
Removes custom settings from chrome.storage.local (apiKey, apiBaseUrl, modelAlias). Only called when switching TO "claude" mode.

chrome.tabs.create override (lines 221-244)
Intercepts https://claude.ai/oauth/authorize → replaces with cfcBase, replaces hardcoded extension ID with chrome.runtime.id, appends &v=version. Also intercepts upgrade URL.

onMessageExternal (lines 246-278)
Overrides sender.origin to always be "https://claude.ai". Handles: ping, _claude_account_mode, _api_key_mode, _update_options, _set_storage_local, _open_options, _create_tab.

render() for DOM injection (lines 281-303)
In window context: reads ui[location.pathname] → for each entry, does document.querySelector(item.selector).innerHTML = item.html. Runs on DOMContentLoaded + popstate.

matchJsx / remixJsx / setJsx (lines 376-511)
The React JSX interception system:

matchJsx(node, selector) — deep comparison of JSX node against a selector pattern
remixJsx(node, renderNode) — applies uiNodes (prepend/append/replace) to matching nodes
setJsx(n) — hooks into React's jsx/jsxs functions by wrapping them with _jsx which calls remixJsx before rendering. Checks n.jsx.name == "_jsx" to avoid double-hooking.
The export function setJsx(n) — this is an EXPORTED function. It needs to be called by the extension's bundled React code. Cocodem's approach hooks it into the module system.

patchLocales (lines not in my screenshots but referenced)

sidePanel override (lines 355-374)
